title: Breathing Room: Writing for Stillness and Peace
description:
Online Mini-Retreat with James Crews Breathing Room: Writing for Stillness and Peace

Saturday, April 18, 10-12 PT \(1-3 pm ET\)

Join poet and editor James Crews for a supportive and encouraging retreat focusing on rest and peace through writing. We will work from poems and prompts from his latest book, Breathing Room \(available March 17\), and create together in a stress-free and tender space. 

There will be time for sharing what you write, if you wish, but there is no pressure to do so, and this workshop is ideal for writers of all levels and backgrounds.

James Crews is the author of Turning Toward Grief: Reflections on Life, Loss & Appreciation, Breathing Room: Poems of Rest & Retreat, and editor of several bestselling poetry anthologies, including Love Is for All of Us, a collection of LGBTQ\+ love poems co-edited with his husband, Brad Peacock. He has also edited The Wonder of Small Things \(winner of the New England Book Award\), The Path to Kindness \(winner of the Nautilus Award\), and How to Love the World, which has sold over 100,000 copies to date. He has been featured on NPR’s Morning Edition, and in People Magazine, The Boston Globe, The New York Times Magazine, The Sun Magazine, and The Washington Post. James lives with his husband on forty rocky acres in Vermont that they are restoring to a habitat for pollinators and native species. jamescrews.net

Register at http://stcolumbasinverness.org/breathing-room

title: Butter & Egg Days Parade & Festival 2026
description:
Theme: "America's Birthday - Petaluma Style"

*Celebrating 250 years of independence, ingenuity, and small-town pride.*

“Americas’ Birthday – Petaluma Style” celebrates the nation’s 250th Birthday by honoring Petaluma’s deep agricultural roots and hometown spirit. This year’s Butter & Egg Days Parade recognizes the farmers, families, immigrants, makers, entrepreneurs, and creatives whose hard work, imagination, and ingenuity reflect the enduring American Dream. This celebration also pays respect to the Indigenous peoples who first stewarded this land, the courage of our founders, and the dedication of the dairy and egg farming community that shaped our town. Rooted in community, innovation, and independence, the parade celebrates the small-town spirit that continues to make Petaluma a vibrant place to call home. Head to Downtown Petaluma and celebrate with our community on this day of fun, history, and local pride!

Parade participants incorporate the theme *“America's Birthday - Petaluma Style”* into their entry design. The theme gives nonprofits, businesses, organizations, and individuals lots of options for showing off their creativity in their designs. All parade entries will be judged on how well their entry portrays this year's theme - winners announced on the website! Check back later to see which entries take home the prizes and earn bragging rights.

The Butter & Egg Days festivities kick off on Saturday, **April 11** with the **Opening Ceremonies** at the Petaluma Historical Library and Museum (20 Fourth St), from Noon to 1pm. Mayor Kevin McDonnell will read a proclamation honoring the Grand Marshal and Good Egg. Come enjoy this display that shows the heart of our community.

One week later on Saturday, **April 18,** the Butter & Egg Days **Parade** steps off at noon and marches through the historic downtown. The parade showcases over 100 units with approximately 3,000 participants and 200 volunteers. Clover Sonoma returns to lead the Clover **Kids’ Parade**, which precedes the main parade at 11:30am with a procession of preschoolers and primary grade youngsters and their families.

The parade is surrounded by a **Festival** that spreads over four city blocks from 10am-5pm offering a wide variety of food, crafts, beverage gardens, two large kid areas, live music, and more! This annual event aims to bring together the community for a day of fun and entertainment.

The following weekend, Downtown Petaluma continues the celebration with the Annual Spring Antique Faire, on Sunday, **April 26**.

Happy Butter & Egg Days!!!

Visit ButterAndEggDays.com for more information!

title: Dumpling Workshop with Lani Chan at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
description:
Join us for a 3-hour hands-on dumpling workshop led by Lani Chan, founder of Hei Ma, where you'll learn to make dumplings entirely from scratch — wrappers, fillings, and all. You'll start by making the dough using heirloom grain flours grown by our Sebastopol neighbor Farmer Mai, who will be on hand to share the story behind their remarkable grains. From there, you'll form and cook vegetarian dumplings, learn to make scallion pancakes, and pair everything with Hei Ma chili crisp and a special dipping sauce made with Gold Ridge Organic Farms Apple Cider Balsamic Vinegar.

The experience begins with a ride aboard our apple-themed trolley out to the Apple Cottage, where the class will take place surrounded by the beauty of the farm. Each guest will receive an apple-blossom pink apron to take home and enjoy a refreshing citrus shrub alongside their freshly made dumplings. Whether you're a seasoned home cook or a first-time dumpling maker, this is an experience you won't forget — good food, great company, and a deeper connection to the ingredients grown right here in Sonoma County.

Lani Chan is the co-founder of Hei Ma \(formerly known as Big Spoon Sauce Co.\), a Sonoma County-based small-batch sauce brand rooted in Chinese culinary tradition and peak-season California produce. What began as a chili crisp project in a Brooklyn apartment in 2019 has grown into a community-driven food brand celebrated for its bold flavors and cultural heart.

Mai Nguyen is an award-winning heirloom grain farmer, miller, seed keeper, and community organizer based right here in Sebastopol. In 2024, their work was recognized with the prestigious James Beard Leadership Award for their contributions to sustainability, equity, and justice in food systems, collaborating with communities and coalitions to shape food policy that uplifts marginalized farmers and promotes land sovereignty.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Small Wonders
description:
Call for Art: Small Wonders

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

\- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

\- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

\- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed (144 sq in) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

\- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired (no alligator clips). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

\- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

Key Dates:

\- Entry Deadline: May 10, 2026 (9 PM)

\- Notification of Selection: By May 13, 2026

\- Shipped Work Deadline: Wednesday, May 27, 2026 (must include pre-paid return label)

\- Hand-Delivery: Sunday, May 31 (12–4 PM) and Monday, June 1 (11 AM–1 PM)

\- Exhibition Dates: June 4, 2026 – July 19, 2026

\- Opening Reception: Saturday, June 6, 2026 (4–6 PM)

\- Pick-up/Return Shipping: July 19 (12–4 PM) and July 20 (11 AM–1 PM); shipping the week of July 20.

Entry Fees:

\- Non-Members: $50 (1 entry), $55 (2 entries), $60 (3 entries). Includes a $60 yearly supporter membership.

\- Current Members: $40 (1 entry), $45 (2 entries), $50 (3 entries).

In this 2 week introductory course, participants will learn a unique approach to watercolor, intended to alleviate the frustration that many experience when learning this beautiful yet challenging medium. 

The class will practice basic drawing in addition to watercolor technique, with a focus on strengthening one’s observational skills while learning a step by step layering process that trains the artist to see value and color.

Our unifying subject will be seasonal produce - fruits, veggies and herbs, that we will render from life. These subjects are great for beginners and experienced watercolor painters alike; their organic shapes make them forgiving drawing subjects, but their beauty can be a muse for life.

All experience levels welcome and all materials provided.

Families are welcome at the ceremonies, which honor the independence and companionship that GDB’s guide dogs provide for GDB’s clients who are blind or visually impaired. The events also allow GDB’s clients to meet the puppy raisers who cared for their canine heroes prior to beginning formal training at GDB’s campus. Ceremonies also recognize recent graduates of GDB’s Orientation and Mobility \(O&M\) Program, K9 Buddy Program, and Breeder Dog Program.

Admission is free, and Kleenex will be provided. Pre-registered bus groups are welcome. Public tours of the campus are offered on the days of the ceremonies. Visit www.guidedogs.com for more information. Graduation events are also livestreamed at https://www.youtube.com/@gdb\_official/streams.

title: Petaluma River High Tide Upstream Paddle
description:
When the tide is high, the Petaluma River opens into a quieter, greener world.

Join The Floathouse crew for a gentle, guided paddle upstream, timed to higher tides that allow access beyond the downtown channel and into a tranquil tidal slough. With extra water beneath us, we’re able to glide into calm, lush stretches of the river that are normally out of reach.

This unhurried paddle highlights the natural beauty of the Petaluma River’s brackish, tidal waterway. Watch for great egrets, blue herons, snowy egrets, turtles basking along the banks, and abundant plant life. The calm water and peaceful surroundings create a deeply grounding experience—many guests say they feel their stress melt away within minutes.

Along the way, knowledgeable guides share stories of the river’s ecology and human history, offering insight into how this upper channel has shaped—and continues to shape—Petaluma. It’s a rare opportunity to experience how close wild nature lives to the heart of downtown.

Beginner-friendly. Sit-on-top kayaks and all gear provided.

title: Calistoga Art Center's Annual Souper Bowl #16
description:
CALISTOGA (February 21, 2026) – Now in its 16th year, Calistoga Art Center’s popular Souper Bowl fundraiser will be held on Saturday, April 18, at the Boys & Girls Club of Calistoga.  Tickets are now on sale, and event sponsorships are available.

Souper Bowl gets its name from the unique pairing of gourmet soups from local restaurants with handmade ceramic bowls crafted by CAC’s talented instructors and students. Guests choose from over 250 artisan bowls which they take home at the end of the evening. Many prize their collection of bowls from past events. Each year, Souper Bowl guests vote for their favorite soup of the night. Last year’s winner was Lovina for its luscious asparagus bisque. 

Souper Bowl 2026 will be more exciting than ever. Guests will bid on a dazzling collection of live and silent auction items as well as enjoy Calistoga AVA wines and desserts. Here’s a “taste” of the items up for auction: A staycation at a private residence at the Four Seasons; a private Sip & Paint party at Calistoga Art Center, curated wine collections and tastings, special dining experiences, fine art and craft pieces in various media, and more.

Proceeds from the event will directly support ongoing art programs for the community, including those designed for children, teens, and seniors. Funds raised will also help cover administrative expenses to operate the CAC as well as critical capital improvements to its facility. 

Tickets are $125 each and available online at www.calistogaartcenter.org/events or by calling 707-942-2278. Each event ticket includes a handmade ceramic bowl to take home, an unlimited soup tasting, charcuterie, bread, and cookies. Wine tickets will be available for purchase. Each guest will be assigned a designated table to ensure smooth and organized seating and you can request seating with friends.  Creative center pieces and table numbers will be designed by CAC students.

title: Sonoma County Philharmonic in concert - FANNY, FLORENCE & SAM
description:
Norman Gamboa, conductor

Esther Rayo, soprano

SAMUEL COLERIDGE-TAYLOR Idyll, Op.44 

FANNY MENDELSSOHN Hero und Leander

FLORENCE PRICE Symphony No. 1  

Join us for a program featuring three under- appreciated composers whose works are finally receiving the attention they deserve.

 ♪ Samuel Coleridge-Taylor’s lovely Idyll sets a reflective and poetic tone with its tender melodies and pastoral elegance.

♪ Fanny Mendelssohn’s dramatic cantata, Hero und Leander, weaves a tragic Greek myth into music of passion and vivid orchestration.

♪ Florence Price’s groundbreaking Symphony No. 1 blends classical forms with African American spirituals and folk rhythms creating an iconic 20th century American masterpiece. 

​Come celebrate the breadth of orchestral music and its enduring power to surprise, delight, and move the human spirit!

title: JaM Cellars Presents Sierra Hull with support from Mason Via
description:
APRIL 18, 2026
PURCHASE TICKETS HERE  
Doors 7pm/ Show 8pm
Ages: 12+ 
Sierra Hull is a seven-time IBMA Mandolin Player of the Year and six-time Grammy nominee, one of bluegrass and Americana’s most dynamic voices. Her latest album, A Tip Toe High Wire, her first independent release, highlights her songwriting and instrumental mastery, featuring Béla Fleck, Tim O’Brien, and Aoife O’Donovan. The album is nominated for four GRAMMY Awards, balancing tradition with innovation. 
Hull has shared stages with Alison Krauss, Eric Clapton, Sturgill Simpson, Slash, and Robert Randolph, and performed on NPR’s Tiny Desk and The Kelly Clarkson Show. She is the first female artist with a Gibson signature mandolin and a Tennessee Governor’s Distinguished Arts Award recipient. 
With support from Mason Via 
Mason Via’s new single, “Wide Open.” Co-written by Mason Via and Zach John King , this track paints vivid pictures of campfires, screen doors, and sunsets over pastures, while also capturing the essence of young heartbreak. Raised in Patrick Springs, VA, Mason drew on his childhood experiences growing up in the hills, hollers, and backwoods of southern Virginia to inspire this incredible new song. Via says, “The song chronicles the singer’s emotional state as he reaches back into his memory to recall how much he loved the girl who has left him, and how much her absence has cut him to the core.” This song evokes a similiar emotion that Mason conveyed in Daughter of the Highlands (his stand out vocal on the Grammy nominated album Jubilee.) The track features Mason Via on lead vocals and guitar; Aaron Ramsey on mandolin; Jason Davis on banjo; Jim Vancleve on fiddle; Jeff Partin on bass and resophonic guitar; Kyser George on second guitar; Brooks Forsyth on harmony vocals; and Nick Goad on harmony vocals. This track sounds like Old Crow Medicine Show, Tyler Childers , Zach Bryan, Flatland Cavalry, Turnpike Troubadours, and Mountain Heart.

title: Helen Putnam Hike with dogs
description:
Go Wild Hikers
Time for a South County hike. Helen Putnam Regional Park is a compact wilderness park featuring beautiful oak savanna, grasslands, and ridges with panoramic views of the Petaluma Valley to the east and the Chileno Valley to the west.

**Where We Meet**
Helen Putnam Park **Chileno Valley parking lot**
411 Chileno Valley Road
Petaluma, CA 94952
Give yourself enough time to arrive, use the restroom & pay park fee. It often takes longer than you think.

**The Hike (Group Hike #340)**
Ridge, Filaree, Pomo, Panorama and Savanna trails - a loop hike
Length - +/-4.75 miles/+/-7.6 kilometers
Elevation change - +/-500 feet/+/-152 meters
Difficulty - 5/10 - easy
Exposures - 70% sun / 30 % shade - poison oak, ticks/insects and views.
Bring plenty of water. At least 34 oz./1 liter!
Dogs - Yes, well behaved and on a leash.
Facilities at trail head - shade, picnic tables and toilets
Cost - $5 cash.
Parking - $8 Sonoma County Regional Parks fee, free with Regional Park pass or limited parking on Chileno Valley Rd.
Remember to wear appropriate hiking shoes, bring plenty of water for your dog too, a hat, snack, layered clothing.
Please Do Not Use Any scented products the day of a group hike!
Of course we will all look out for each other but ultimately, hikers are responsible for their own safety and well-being during hikes.

title: INTO THE LIGHT: Light-filled aintings by Katy Boggs
description:
Katy's paintings are an exploration of light—how it shapes form, reveals color, and defines what we see.

"I am drawn to moments where light is felt as much as seen: filtering through dense leaves, towering in the crowns of trees, glinting off cresting waves, or softening into the quiet glow of a sunset. Light is everywhere; without it, there is no seeing. Beyond its physical presence, it also carries a deeper resonance as a symbol of hope. In a time of uncertainty, this work seeks to bring light into the image, both visually and metaphorically."

Reception: April 25, 4 to 6 pm.

title: Wood Engraving - 2 Day Intensive Workshop
description:
This two-day workshop introduces the art and practice of wood engraving. The hard woods used to make wood engraving blocks are type-high (.918”, the height of metal type) and are cut across the grain rather than parallel to it like wood cuts. These durable end-grain blocks allow for extensive detail. The tools used are gravers (or burins) that are different than the gouge tools used for wood cuts. This versatile form of printmaking requires little space and minimal equipment and is perfect for a small home studio.

Day 1: We will start with a brief history of wood engraving including its long relationship to letterpress printing, and we will study examples of period and contemporary wood engravings. Students will begin with a sampler block to explore the effects of various tools, proof the block on the press, and transfer a design onto another block to consider the approach for their first engraving.

Day 2: Students will learn how to sharpen their gravers and continue to engrave their blocks. We will become familiar with basic use of the Vandercook SP-15 cylinder press to ink and proof the block and troubleshoot issues when printing. Printing an edition of a block will be discussed, and those wanting to contribute a print to the workshop portfolio are encouraged to do so. Students will leave the workshop with the skills to master the graver tool to create intricate prints, a value test block for future reference, an instructive handout, a block to edition, and a portfolio of workshop prints.

Level: Beginner – no previous experience necessary

*Includes $50 materials fee, which covers #3 elliptical tint tool and two 3”x 4” end-grain maple blocks)*

**INSTRUCTOR**

**Colleen Dwire** initially learned wood engraving in a workshop with American Master John DePol and has been practicing for over thirty years. She exhibits her prints internationally. Colleen is an elected member of the Society of Wood Engravers (UK) and serves as Secretary and Exhibitions Officer for Wood Engravers’ Network (USA) and as a board member of North Bay Letterpress Arts. Learn more at www.colleendwire.com and follow on colleendwire.bsky.social.

title: World Dance
description:
Travel the World—No Passport Required!

Every Sunday at 10:00 AM, grab your global one-way ticket to fitness. We’re traveling across continents through rhythm and movement, blending high-energy world dances with a full-body workout. Whether you’re a seasoned pro or have two left feet, come sweat, smile, and discover your new favorite beat.

Who: All adult ages and skill levels.

When: Sundays @ 10:00 AM.

The Vibe: Pure fun, global rhythms, and a community that moves together.

About Zeena

Zeena Quinn’s World Dance classes are based on learning coordination, motivating the brain, dance techniques, and therefore, mind-body transformation. By creating a supportive system, participants discover themselves in their own way via dance.

Participants will work upper and lower body, cardio and mostly rhythms & coordination. One will understand and learn to identify the different rhythms while having fun! Zeena has a lifetime of experience in dance, professional performance, choreography, teaching, as well as, in fitness and resistance training.

Zeena has toured the Bay Area presenting a variety of American swing, Charlston, hip hop, disco, line dances, and international dance styles such as Bollywood, Afro-Brazilian/Samba, Flamenco, and European and Eastern Folk. These authentic dance techniques demonstrate how our body is an instrument. Because of her extensive range of dance training, she brings the authenticity of technique into her vibrant teaching style.

Come take a trip around theworld! Comfortable clothes and worn shoes that tie. No Hoka or hiking shoes please.

In this workshop, French-American collage artist Catherine Cruz guides you in creating a cohesive series of abstract collages on four wood panels, exploring color, line, shape, design principles, and paper-mounting techniques.

About the Class

In this workshop, French-American collage artist Catherine Cruz will teach you how to create a dynamic series of abstract collages using elements such as color, line and shape. You will work on four small wood panels to compose a cohesive series. Working on several panels at once offers several advantages, including greater creative momentum, the ability to build a strong thematic connection between pieces, and a way to maintain creative flow. This technique allows for a deeper exploration of an idea or theme than is possible with a single piece. We will start with short composition exercises to discuss design principles and abstraction. Then Catherine will demonstrate her method for mounting papers on the panels. You will have ample time to select papers and create your designs. We will take a short break for lunch between 12:30 and 1:00 pm so please bring your lunch and a beverage. What you’ll learn from this workshop:

Reliable method for layering collage papers

Creative ways to explore abstraction

Techniques for creating a cohesive series

Strategies for refining your composition

IMPORTANT: Each participant must purchase and bring four 6”x6” cradled wood panels to the workshop. Instructions for where to purchase your panels and how to prepare them will be provided upon registration.

Instructor will provide: a wide assortment of painted and printed collage papers, brushes, acrylic medium, scissors, rulers.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Small Wonders
description:
Call for Art: Small Wonders

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

\- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

\- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

\- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed (144 sq in) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

\- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired (no alligator clips). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

\- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

Key Dates:

\- Entry Deadline: May 10, 2026 (9 PM)

\- Notification of Selection: By May 13, 2026

\- Shipped Work Deadline: Wednesday, May 27, 2026 (must include pre-paid return label)

\- Hand-Delivery: Sunday, May 31 (12–4 PM) and Monday, June 1 (11 AM–1 PM)

\- Exhibition Dates: June 4, 2026 – July 19, 2026

\- Opening Reception: Saturday, June 6, 2026 (4–6 PM)

\- Pick-up/Return Shipping: July 19 (12–4 PM) and July 20 (11 AM–1 PM); shipping the week of July 20.

Entry Fees:

\- Non-Members: $50 (1 entry), $55 (2 entries), $60 (3 entries). Includes a $60 yearly supporter membership.

\- Current Members: $40 (1 entry), $45 (2 entries), $50 (3 entries).

This curated experience brings together sweeping views, unreleased barrel tastings, and relaxed, thoughtful hospitality — all led by winemaker Doug Hackett himself.

You’ll begin with a welcome wine and bites as you take in the breathtaking scenery, followed by an intimate barrel tasting of unreleased wines from Spicy Vines and Pine Mountain Vineyards. Afterward, we’ll settle in for a laid-back BBQ lunch, generous pours, and easy conversation — the kind that only happens when you slow down and savor where you are.

This isn’t just another tasting. It’s a rare opportunity to experience Pine Mountain in a way few ever do.

They specialize in Pinot Noir, Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel, and Chardonnay. You are welcome to purchase wine outside of the tasting provided.

There is a maximum of 15 spots available, and this is a Co-ed event, so both men and women are welcome.

The cost of the event is $26, which includes the wine tasting, plus our club slush fund fee of $1. They likely will waive the tasting fee with the purchase of wine bottles, or by becoming members of their wine club.

Guests are welcome. I suggest you wear layers as we will be outside, and sometimes the weather is windy or cold. Please allow extra time to get there, the vineyard is about 5 miles from the Highway 101 exit at Lytton. We will confirm headcount about a week before.

Cheers to this fun relaxing event!

title: Lauren Jenkins
description:
Americana singer-songwriter Lauren Jenkins has been a touring artist since she was 15 years old. The Texas born, Carolina-raised artist chose a life that would fit perfectly in the songs she writes: across countless smoky bars, fake IDs, and endless miles on the road, music has been her one constant companion. Named an Artist to Watch by the New York Times, Billboard, Rolling Stone, Pandora, and many more, she was also chosen as a member of the “Class of 2019” by influential radio DJ Bobby Bones, and made her TODAY Show debut as Elvis Duran’s Artist of the Month. An accomplished actress and filmmaker, Lauren wrote, produced, and starred in an original short film titled 'Running Out of Road' that accompanied the release of her critically-acclaimed debut album, NO SAINT,  on Big Machine Records. Her short film"Running Out Of Road" was an official selection at Roswell Film Festival and screened during the Nashville Film Festival, SXSW, and Sundance. 

She has hosted as a Guest DJ on Sirius XM's E Street channel. Her love of Bruce Springsteen compelled her to record two of the Bosses songs "Stolen Car" and "Hungry Heart", which also debuted on the E Street Channel. 

Lauren has built a loyal following in Europe and the UK after her debut at C2C festival in March of 2019. Just before the world shut down in 2020 Lauren was just coming home from a successiful tour in Europe and the UK. 

Since the pandemic, Lauren has been connecting with audiences through virtual "living room concerts" until she can get back on the road. 

In May of 2020, she released “Ain’t That Hard,” her first song as a fully independent artist. Part 1 of her sophomore record "Miles On Me" is out now.

"“Lauren is unapologetically raw at times, uncompromising and unflinching in the way she looks at the world and herself. If you are looking for someone with meaning, someone with a knack for melody and someone with an honest, authentic view of life, love and relationships, then Lauren Jenkins always has been, and even more now, is the perfect artist for you.” - Lyric Magazine

title: Slow Wildflower Journey
description:
Do you enjoy a slow walk in a valley, breezes, wildflowers, the sounds of songbirds, the taste of a Douglas Fir needle or a California Bay leaf, the aroma of Tarweed, or watching wild turkeys and California Quail hunt for seeds and insects in the grass? Join Certified California Naturalists and Sugarloaf docents for this series of meandering Sunday afternoon explorations. Each month (weather permitting) we will explore one or two of our accessible trails-- the Creekside Nature Trail, and the Meadow Trail. Suitable for all levels and a range of mobility, these Sunday afternoon adventures will accommodate people using walkers or wheelchairs, young children, parents with babies in strollers, as well as those who just enjoy slow walks in nature that stimulate the five senses. Our April outing will focus on the wildflowers of Sugarloaf.

Tickets are $5 for adults and free for children under 18 years of age (a parent or legal guardian must accompany minors). Meet at the White Barn parking lot. There will be frequent stops and opportunities for conversation, photography, nature journaling, wildlife viewing, resting, etc., so bring your nature journal, camera, or binoculars if you have them. Wear comfortable shoes, a hat, sun protection, bring water and if desired, a snack. Parking fees apply. Rain cancel. In the event of rain, we will reschedule to Sunday, April 12, at the same time.

title: Sonoma County Philharmonic in concert - FANNY, FLORENCE & SAM
description:
Norman Gamboa, conductor

Esther Rayo, soprano

SAMUEL COLERIDGE-TAYLOR Idyll, Op.44 

FANNY MENDELSSOHN Hero und Leander

FLORENCE PRICE Symphony No. 1  

Join us for a program featuring three under- appreciated composers whose works are finally receiving the attention they deserve.

 ♪ Samuel Coleridge-Taylor’s lovely Idyll sets a reflective and poetic tone with its tender melodies and pastoral elegance.

♪ Fanny Mendelssohn’s dramatic cantata, Hero und Leander, weaves a tragic Greek myth into music of passion and vivid orchestration.

♪ Florence Price’s groundbreaking Symphony No. 1 blends classical forms with African American spirituals and folk rhythms creating an iconic 20th century American masterpiece. 

​Come celebrate the breadth of orchestral music and its enduring power to surprise, delight, and move the human spirit!

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting in Santa Rosa
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

Blanchard will play these compositions: Marcello's Psalm 19 and Bohm's 3 settings of Vater unser in Himmelreich \(Lord's Prayer\); J.S. Bach's Vom Himmel Hoch and his Ascension by Messiaen's Priere du Christ \(Ascension Suite, No. IV\); Thomas Fielding's Versets on Veni Creator \(w chanted verses\), and Weckmann's O Lux Beata Trinitas.

title: What About Age? Art Exhibit
description:
*What About Age?* art exhibit has arrived in Marin County! Originally displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows, this exhibit explores ageism through contemporary art, featuring works by both local youth and senior artists.

*What About Age?* is an art exhibit and educational initiative designed to challenge stereotypes about aging, address ageism and social isolation, and promote intergenerational dialogue through the lens of art.

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

title: INTO THE LIGHT: Light-filled aintings by Katy Boggs
description:
Katy's paintings are an exploration of light—how it shapes form, reveals color, and defines what we see.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Small Wonders
description:
Call for Art: Small Wonders

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

\- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

\- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

\- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed (144 sq in) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

\- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired (no alligator clips). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

\- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

Key Dates:

\- Entry Deadline: May 10, 2026 (9 PM)

\- Notification of Selection: By May 13, 2026

\- Shipped Work Deadline: Wednesday, May 27, 2026 (must include pre-paid return label)

\- Hand-Delivery: Sunday, May 31 (12–4 PM) and Monday, June 1 (11 AM–1 PM)

\- Exhibition Dates: June 4, 2026 – July 19, 2026

\- Opening Reception: Saturday, June 6, 2026 (4–6 PM)

\- Pick-up/Return Shipping: July 19 (12–4 PM) and July 20 (11 AM–1 PM); shipping the week of July 20.

Entry Fees:

\- Non-Members: $50 (1 entry), $55 (2 entries), $60 (3 entries). Includes a $60 yearly supporter membership.

\- Current Members: $40 (1 entry), $45 (2 entries), $50 (3 entries).

title: An Evening with MATISYAHU
description:
April 20, 2026
PURCHASE TICKETS HERE  
Doors 7pm/ Show 8pm
Ages: 12+ 





There is a spirit that hovers above the waters. It has been here since the beginning of creation, yet it is just being born. Ancient Child is Matisyahu’s 8th full length studio album. In Jewish mysticism, eight is the number beyond the natural cycle of the physical world.  As Matisyahu brings forth his eighth studio album, the Ancient Child simultaneously reaches back in time and towards the future, in search of the infinite divine light of redemption. Here, Matisyahu finds himself reconnected with his Jewish identity and spirituality in a world post October 7th. 
In a climate that has become obsessed with being “right” and defending its ego at all costs, the Ancient Child investigates questions about history, identity and destiny from the humility of a child through the wisdom of the of generations’ past. While Matisyahu had shifted his focus over the last decade to his personal life from his religion, Ancient Child is a strong return to his love for Judaism and the deep existential quest to find universal meaning in the darkness.So what does Matisyahu come up with? 










When the world turns to darkness, humanity has a choice – hide in a corner or meet at the crossroads and find a way to come together. As Matisyahu sings in “Find A Way” 
I’m at the crossroads if you wanna partake 
But make no mistake 
If you participate 
There’s no one you can escape 
Pontificate upon it 
And get caught in a maze 
Of confuse-ment… 
…I’ll Find a Way 
It’s hard work, but when we unite, the entire world is forever changed for the better.  From here the Ancient Child is born. From here the humility of the child and the wisdom of the elders offer a glimpse at a redemptive future. The music on this album is not reggae. It’s not rock. It’s not hip hop. Yet it will be called all these things. Like Matisyahu, and the world he tries to create lyrically, it is a melding of various styles and sounds that have been influential from a universe of music the singer has absorbed through more than twenty years as a recording and touring Artist. 
As a true artist, Matisyahu is not concerned with reproducing the sounds of a specific genre but only interested in what moves the emotion and prepares the runway for his concepts to be cleared for landing. He writes from his experiences about hopes, challenges and fears. Authenticity is always at the core.   
In a reference the album’s title, Matisyahu presents a meditation on Jewish history, his own role as a father, and his yearning for a better future, where the metaphorical sun/son comes up to move beyond the limitations.

title: What About Age? Art Exhibit
description:
*What About Age?* art exhibit has arrived in Marin County! Originally displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows, this exhibit explores ageism through contemporary art, featuring works by both local youth and senior artists.

*What About Age?* is an art exhibit and educational initiative designed to challenge stereotypes about aging, address ageism and social isolation, and promote intergenerational dialogue through the lens of art.

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Small Wonders
description:
Call for Art: Small Wonders

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

\- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

\- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

\- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed (144 sq in) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

\- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired (no alligator clips). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

\- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

Key Dates:

\- Entry Deadline: May 10, 2026 (9 PM)

\- Notification of Selection: By May 13, 2026

\- Shipped Work Deadline: Wednesday, May 27, 2026 (must include pre-paid return label)

\- Hand-Delivery: Sunday, May 31 (12–4 PM) and Monday, June 1 (11 AM–1 PM)

\- Exhibition Dates: June 4, 2026 – July 19, 2026

\- Opening Reception: Saturday, June 6, 2026 (4–6 PM)

\- Pick-up/Return Shipping: July 19 (12–4 PM) and July 20 (11 AM–1 PM); shipping the week of July 20.

Entry Fees:

\- Non-Members: $50 (1 entry), $55 (2 entries), $60 (3 entries). Includes a $60 yearly supporter membership.

\- Current Members: $40 (1 entry), $45 (2 entries), $50 (3 entries).

This class focuses on the simple delight of mixing color with water, brushing it on paper, and watching what happens as it moves and dries. You will learn easy ways to create paintings that are all about color and the sometimes unpredictable nature of water.

$30 – Per Family, max of 3 people. Learn ancient stick loom weaving in this hands-on class. Create a beautiful tapestry using natural materials, simple techniques, and your choice of colors.

About the Class

Come learn the ancient craft of weaving with a stick loom! In this family-friendly class, you’ll learn to hand-weave a simple tapestry using sticks as your loom. The demonstration will include setting up the warp threads, learning a simple over-under stitch pattern and the final knot step. There will be a variety of stick shapes to choose from and plenty of room to play with pattern and color. And voila! You’ll leave the class with your stick-loom tapestry \(either in progress or completed, depending on the chosen scale\). Hang your weaving on your wall to bring nature indoors or from a tree to bring your artistry outside! This class is open to parents with their children ages 7 through 12.

description:
Schedule

Experience Level

Beginning

Printmaking

Age\(s\)

16\+

$195 – Registration Cost $30 – Materials Fee $225 – Total Registration CostWhat exactly is printmaking? We invite you into our print studio to experience a beginner’s journey through this incredible art form

What you’ll do

What is printmaking? We invite you into our print studio to experience a fun beginner’s journey through this incredible art form in five paced weeks. Join Kelly in this unique introduction to print through the world of monotype, relief, intaglio and stencil screenprinting. This popular multi-session workshop is only taught twice per year in the spring and fall seasons. Students will try various techniques in this guided, hands-on class to create a beginning portfolio of prints. Learn a basic understanding of the four classic methods within the family of printmaking and gain access to our member’s print studio to continue working on your own projects. This class is perfect for absolute beginners or even experienced artists who may need a refresher course in printmaking. 

Monotype – Create a single print on a flat matrix using ink and a variety of marks and  textures

Relief – Carve, ink and block print using a mini speedy carve block and a linocut tool

Intaglio – Draw, scratch and ink onto a surface to roll out a creative print using a small press

Stencil – Pull a silkscreen and learn to transfer a flat stencil to make a colorful printed impression

No prior printmaking experience is necessary. This class requires hand dexterity to maneuver carving tools and studio equipment. Students must feel comfortable handling machinery.

You don't consider yourself “naturally” quick, funny or outgoing? Perfect! You don't need to be to do improv, all you need to do is show up--truly! You will surprise yourself, then watch your confidence grow. Improv tools can help us be more comfortable with ourselves, thus enabling us to be more relaxed and engaged in our work, social situations or onstage, for those who perform or wish to.

Mostly it’s just really, really fun!

title: JaM Cellars Presents The Wallflowers with support from  Aaron Lee Tasjan
description:
April 21, 2026
PURCHASE TICKETS HERE  
Doors 7pm/ Show 8pm
Ages: 12+ 
with support from Aaron Lee Tasjan 
The Wallflowers will mark the 30th anniversary of their landmark album Bringing Down the Horse with a nationwide U.S. tour kicking off April 17, 2026. The band will perform their classic album in its entirety, in sequence. The tour will also include a performance at Stagecoach, the world’s largest country music festival. 
Originally released on May 21, 1996, Bringing Down the Horse was a critical and commercial triumph. The album peaked at number four on the Billboard 200 and was certified quadruple platinum, cementing the band’s place in ’90s rock history. The LP yielded four hit singles: 
• “6th Avenue Heartache” – Two Grammy nominations (1997)• “One Headlight” – Reached #1 on the Billboard singles chart, winning two Grammy Awards (1998). The song ranked #58 on Rolling Stone’s “100 Greatest Pop Songs”• “The Difference” – Grammy nomination (1998)• “Three Marlenas” – Released as the album’s final single in October 1997 
Influenced by a slew of first-generation American songwriters including The Band and Tom Petty & the Heartbreakers, The Wallflowers will also pay tribute on the upcoming tour to the 50th anniversary of Tom Petty & the Heartbreakers by playing Petty’s 1982 album Long After Dark in its entirety and in sequence as well. 
Jakob Dylan, the band’s chief songwriter, remains a vital performer in American rock music. As part of three decades of work, in 2002 he inducted Tom Petty into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. In 2018, he performed in the critically acclaimed documentary Echo in the Canyon, collaborating with artists ranging from Neil Young and Eric Clapton to Beck, Cat Power, Norah Jones, and Regina Spektor. 
Dylan also contributed songs to several soundtracks, including The Wallflowers’ cover of “Heroes” for the 1998 Godzillafilm soundtrack; “Arms of a Ghost” to the television series NCIS: Los Angeles; and “Nothing But the Whole Wide World” to Friday Night Lights. In 2025 The Wallflowers supported Eric Clapton on his U.S. tour, as they have done in the past, as well as supporting performances for The Who and The Rolling Stones. 
For tour dates, tickets, and additional updates, visit www.wallflowersmusic.com.

description: Regenerative Ayurvedic Yoga with Tirza Dawn Come, step onto your mat with an open heart and an open mind. Invest in your self care and join us for morning yoga in the OCA studio. $20 per class, $15 for OCA members. Each Wednesday from 9:00-10:15 AM in our Studio. Pay at the door for a-la-carte sessions or use the links below to pay ahead for four weeks at a time.  Pay Online 4 sessions - OCA members  Pay Online 4 sessions - non members Tirza Dawn Naramore is a yogi, mother, artist, ceremonialist and lover of life. She has been practicing and teaching yoga and meditation for 30 years and offers yoga retreats and trainings that center on optimum health, self realization and self love. Her teachers are from many yoga and tantric traditions, but her primary lineages are Iyengar and Kali Ray.  Tirza is deeply devoted to community building and is honored to have created a number of community supported non profits including Mystic Family Circus and The AWAKEN Project, which serves families with children on the autism spectrum. Tirza is proud to be the mother of 3 wild teenagers, including her incredible son who is diagnosed with autism. Tirza's spirituality is one of many influences and teachings. Beginning with a Christian up-bringing and being raised on a Christian commune in her early childhood, she later expanded into more earth-based ways. While in her 20's Tirza was adopted into the Native American Church, where she learned from her relatives a way of living the "Beauty Way." During the 1990's and early 2000's, Tirza lived in San Francisco, Oakland and Berkeley, directing the Mystic Family Circus, which was a performance group dedicated to cultural awareness and bridge building. She worked with Cirque du Soleil, Burning Man, Reclaiming, Contraband, CELLspace and other Bay Area art collectives and non profits to provide conscious entertainment and "prayerformances" for the betterment of humankind and the planet. In 2012, Tirza helped to found the Buckeye Gathering, an ancestral skills gathering in Northern California which draws teachers and students of all ages to learn ancestral ways of tending the earth and survival skills. Tirza Dawn was the founder of yoga programming and the Ayurvedic Yoga Teacher Trainings at the dhyana Center of Ayurveda in Sebastopol, California, which operated a community center of healing and education from 2010 to 2020.

title: What About Age? Art Exhibit
description:
*What About Age?* art exhibit has arrived in Marin County! Originally displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows, this exhibit explores ageism through contemporary art, featuring works by both local youth and senior artists.

*What About Age?* is an art exhibit and educational initiative designed to challenge stereotypes about aging, address ageism and social isolation, and promote intergenerational dialogue through the lens of art.

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Small Wonders
description:
Call for Art: Small Wonders

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

\- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

\- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

\- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed (144 sq in) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

\- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired (no alligator clips). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

\- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

description: 4 - 18\+ yrs Adult participation optional Class Experience Together, we will breathe and enjoy the feel of our hands creating with colorful textural materials. This class is designed for littles ones and their families to unwind and decompress in the late afternoon and enjoy process art. We will create with a variety of materials that will be set out in an open ended, Reggio Emelia style where students are offered invitations to play with the materials. We will explore different themes such as painting with acrylic or tempera; do collages with various types of paper and mixed media; practice sculpture; or just make creative art with recycled materials. The only assignment is to play and explore with colors, shapes, and textures, with no messy clean-up at home! "Play is a key component of the arts and aesthetics in myriad ways. Art and play are like two sides of the same coin, with play being a part of artistic expression, imagination, creativity, and curiosity." - Susan Magsamen,  Your Brain on Art: How the Arts Transform Us Amanda Rose Hopkins has a Bachelor of Fine Arts from UC Santa Cruz and thereafter she worked as an apprentice artist at the Sarnath International Nyingma Institute, near Varanasi, India. She has been working with children since 2009. She completed a multiple subject teaching credential program and has worked locally at Sunridge Charter School, The REACH School, Sebastopol Center for the Arts and Santa Rosa Junior College. She has studied multicultural education, Positive Discipline, Toolbox and child development. title: Golden Hour Wildflower Hike
description:
Vista Trail is a favorite yearround due to the diversity of habitats along the route to complete the loop. Along the way, we'll see California Poppies and Fairy Lanterns along grasslands, irises along Gray Pine, lupines along Vista, Orange Bush Monkeyflower along Bald Mountain Trail, and Blue-Eyed Grass on Lower Bald Mountain Trail, along with a multitude of other species.

Meet at the White Barn parking lot. Tickets are $10 for general admission, $5 for students, youth (12-17 year olds), Sugarloaf members, Sugarloaf or RFO volunteers, and free for children 7-12. All children under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. This outing is not for children under 7 years old.

Wear appropriate footwear for slippery/rocky trails, bring layers, at least a quart of water, and a flashlight, in case the hike ends later than planned. Parking fees apply.

title: Poetry Month Writing & Printing Workshop Series
description:
Each week, we’ll warm up with guided poetry prompts and group workshopping, then move into spontaneous composition using movable metal and wood type. You’ll set short poems by hand, experiment with layout and typography, and print your work on the press—embracing the beautiful constraints and surprises of letterpress.

As the weeks progress, we’ll curate and print a collaborative chapbook featuring original poems from everyone in the group. The final result will be a shared, tactile publication that reflects a month of creative exchange, ink-stained hands, and collective storytelling.

No prior letterpress or poetry experience is required—just curiosity, openness, and a willingness to play with language and form. Whether you’re a seasoned poet or brand new to writing, this workshop offers space to experiment, connect, and make something meaningful together.

*All materials included. Participants will receive copies of the finished chapbook.*

title: Benefit for Walker Creek Music Camp - An Evening of American Roots Music
description:
Walker Creek Music Camp Presents Teacher Concert Series IV Benefit Concert Celebrating American Roots Music

The concert supports Walker Creek Music Camp’s mission to provide world-class music education and expand access to traditional roots music through classes, youth programs, and scholarships.

The evening will feature these outstanding faculty and alumni performing bluegrass, old-time, jazz, and swing:

Walker Creek All-Stars A “supergroup” of current and former instructors featuring: Yoseff Tucker \(guitar\), Tod Livingston \(dobro\), Bethany Raine Sorkey \(bass\), Paul Shelasky \(fiddle\), Ryan Breen \(banjo\), and Tom Bekeny \(mandolin\).

Hildaland A duo blending Scottish and American traditions featuring fiddler Louise Bichan and mandolin virtuoso Ethan Setiawan.

Pacific Drive A high-energy bluegrass band formed at Walker Creek Music Camp featuring Dana Frankel, David Thiessen, Jesse Fichman, Helen Foley, and Sam Reed.

About Walker Creek Music Camp Founded in 2013, Walker Creek Music Camp is a California nonprofit dedicated to teaching, preserving, and celebrating American roots music. The camp offers world-class instruction for students of all ages and hosts sessions twice each year at Walker Creek Ranch Conference Center.

The camp’s Music & More \(M&M’s\) youth program provides tuition-free instruction for children ages 6–13, along with scholarships and work-trade opportunities that help make music education accessible to all.

More information: walkercreekmusiccamp.org

title: What About Age? Art Exhibit
description:
*What About Age?* art exhibit has arrived in Marin County! Originally displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows, this exhibit explores ageism through contemporary art, featuring works by both local youth and senior artists.

*What About Age?* is an art exhibit and educational initiative designed to challenge stereotypes about aging, address ageism and social isolation, and promote intergenerational dialogue through the lens of art.

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

description:
Katy's paintings are an exploration of light—how it shapes form, reveals color, and defines what we see.

Light is everywhere; without it, there is no seeing. Beyond its physical presence, it also carries a deeper resonance as a symbol of hope. In a time of uncertainty, this work seeks to bring light into the image, both visually and metaphorically."

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net**

description:
Call for Art: Small Wonders

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

\- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

\- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

\- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed (144 sq in) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

\- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired (no alligator clips). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

\- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

Key Dates:

\- Entry Deadline: May 10, 2026 (9 PM)

\- Notification of Selection: By May 13, 2026

\- Shipped Work Deadline: Wednesday, May 27, 2026 (must include pre-paid return label)

\- Hand-Delivery: Sunday, May 31 (12–4 PM) and Monday, June 1 (11 AM–1 PM)

\- Exhibition Dates: June 4, 2026 – July 19, 2026

\- Opening Reception: Saturday, June 6, 2026 (4–6 PM)

\- Pick-up/Return Shipping: July 19 (12–4 PM) and July 20 (11 AM–1 PM); shipping the week of July 20.

Entry Fees:

\- Non-Members: $50 (1 entry), $55 (2 entries), $60 (3 entries). Includes a $60 yearly supporter membership.

\- Current Members: $40 (1 entry), $45 (2 entries), $50 (3 entries).

$25 – One Bag or Doll Entry $40 – Two Bags or Dolls entryTransform plastic dolls and create upcycled bags from trash into unique art. Join our hands-on Trashion workshop for the Gallery 212 Exhibit and Auction.

About the Class

This hands-on workshop invites participants to rescue and reinvent plastic dolls \(Barbies, Kens, and dolls that are under 12 inches\) often destined for landfills, where they can take 20 to 500 years to decompose. As part of Trashion Season, join us for the beloved Gallery 212 Exhibit and Auction \(April 3 – 25\) where discarded materials are transformed into small-scale works of art for a good cause. Together, we’ll reclaim these forgotten figures and reimagine them as expressive, one-of-a-kind artworks for submission to the gallery exhibit and auction. New this year: Bags! In addition to dolls, we’re expanding the exhibit to include bags—think totes, clutches, cross bagsm fanny packs, coin purses, and backpacks. Just like the Trashion runway, the only rule is that your piece must be made from unconventional materials and/or upcycled/used textiles. Participants will have access to access to sewing machines, hot glue guns, irons, hair dryers and other creative tools as well of a wide selection of trash and upcycled materials to bring their vision to life. BYOT \(Bring your own trash\) is also welcome and encouraged! The workshop registration is your application fee to the gallery exhibit! Come play, experiment, and collaborate while contributing to a dynamic gallery exhibit that raises funds for Sonoma Community Center programming through the auction. It’s a joy to see your art find a new home—and to be part of a creative community turning trash into treasure.

Thank you to Recology Sonoma-Marin for donating Barbies & Dolls for our gallery exhibit every year.
