title: Joe Kaplow & Cactus Lee
description:
Before I started my career I had a choice: to take over my parent's thoroughbred farm in New Jersey or pursue music full time in California and relinquish the farm to sale.  I still wonder what life would have looked like had I stayed, but who can resist the gold rush?  Besides, I plan to get back there one day on another farm with some other red barn. 

  

My music comes from life’s moments -- smelling 4 acres of freshly cut grass, watching the steam from a horse's breath in the early morning, finally holding the neck of my guitar after holding bridles and worn wooden handles all day.  4000 acres of freshly burnt wildfire, watching the steam from the Pacific Ocean's breath in the early morning, finally holding the neck of my guitar after clutching the worn steering wheel of the tour van all day.  

Now my reality is in Bonny Doon, CA, where mountains meet the sea. I am in my recording studio, aptly named Hippie Cowboy, every day.  Slow and steady; keep it fun, stay engaged.  All for the moment when the song finally sounds right.  My dad passed away a couple years ago -- his bullwhip is on the wall, his Harley is in the driveway. He visits me in dreams, and oh, the moment I wake up!  Sometimes I write for him. Sometimes for my mom, who I hope will move out to California soon.   Maybe she could volunteer at an equestrian center... 

A person is made from their moments, like their music is made.  I know this is a bio but I shouldn't have to say much.  Listen to the record.  If I've done my job well, you will know me by the end.

title: Alibi April Book Club: Hamnet by Maggie o'Farrell
description:
Please join us on Thursday, April 23rd at 7pm to discuss “Hamnet” by Maggie O’Farrell, the Alibi Book Club ‘s selection for April and Poetry Month. \(I’ll admit — I chose this one because it’s been on my list forever, and I wanted to read it before seeing the film!\)

NEW YORK TIMES BESTSELLER • NATIONAL BOOK CRITICS CIRCLE AWARD WINNER

The acclaimed author of the Reese’s Book Club pick The Marriage Portrait delivers a deeply moving novel about the death of Shakespeare’s eleven-year-old son, Hamnet, and the years leading up to the production of his great play Hamlet.

“Miraculous. . . . Brilliant. . . . A novel told with the urgency of a whispered prayer—or curse. . . . A richly drawn and intimate portrait of 16th-century English life set against the arrival of one devastating death.” —Ron Charles, The Washington Post

England, 1580: The Black Death creeps across the land, an ever-present threat, infecting the healthy, the sick, the old and the young alike. The end of days is near, but life always goes on.

A young Latin tutor—penniless and bullied by a violent father—falls in love with an extraordinary, eccentric young woman. Agnes is a wild creature who walks her family’s land with a falcon on her glove and is known throughout the countryside for her unusual gifts as a healer, understanding plants and potions better than she does people. Once she settles with her husband on Henley Street in Stratford-upon-Avon, she becomes a fiercely protective mother and a steadfast, centrifugal force in the life of her young husband, whose career on the London stage is just taking off when his beloved young son succumbs to sudden fever.

Hamnet is mesmerizing, seductive, impossible to put down–a magnificent leap forward from one of our most gifted novelists.

title: Louise Bichan
location: Walker Creek Ranch Retreat and Conference Center
description:
Louise Bichan is a USA-based Scottish musician and photographer who uses both mediums to tell stories old and new.

Growing up in the remote but culturally rich Orkney islands, a place where creativity abounds and playing music has been a part of the social fabric for centuries, gave Louise a solid grounding in music. She started playing fiddle at the age of 7 after witnessing the magic of live music: “I remember the butterflies in the tummy feeling when watching concerts at the Orkney Folk Festival as a kid, wanting to be a part of it all.” The sense of community and belonging it gave her was infectious; she pestered her parents to let her learn.

In the years since, she has honed her craft, first amongst the cream of Scottish folk at Glasgow’s renowned session scene and performances with talent like Orkney group Fara and award-winning singer-songwriter Rachel Sermanni, before a scholarship to Berklee College of Music, Boston, where she developed her style further.

Masterfully blending traditional and classical arrangements, her music is thoughtful, and complex, curious and playful. She composes in response to her roots and the world around her; weaving through stories of connection, to people, nature, the past and the possibility of the future.

title: Amber Rubarth + Jaimee Harris (21 and Over)
Jaimee Harris & Amber Rubarth
description:
Jaimee Harris turned 30 during the pandemic. It’s a milestone that is a rite of passage even during normal times. But for this Texas-born singer-songwriter, it came in the midst of one of the strangest and most tumultuous periods in American history. When the world stopped during lockdown, Harris, like many others, found herself gazing back into the past, ruminating on the nature of her hometown and family origins, and reckoning with their imprint on her. The term ‘nostalgia’ derives from the Greek words nostos \(return\) and algos \(pain\), and if Harris’s Boomerang Town can be regarded as a nostalgic album, it is only nostalgic in the sense that the longing for home is a desire to return to the past and heal old wounds.

“I’m at an age where I’m wrestling with trying to understand the nature of my family,” Harris says. “There’s been suicide, suicide ideation, and there’s certainly been addiction all through my family. My dad’s father died of suicide when he was 25 and I was 5. I couldn’t imagine not having my dad right now.”

Harris’s sophomore effort, Boomerang Town marks a bold step forward for this country-folk-leaning singer-songwriter. It is an arresting, ambitious song-cycle that explores the generational arc of family, the stranglehold of addiction, and the fragile ties that bind us together as Americans.

For Harris, the album began gestating around 2016, a time of great loss for many in the Americana community, with the songwriter losing several musicians close to her. The shift in the nation’s political landscape had ushered in a new level of polarization that saw whole swaths of cultural life being demonized. For someone who grew up in a small town outside of Waco, Harris believed the values instilled in her by her parents were not entirely in line with how many on the left were viewing — and vilifying — Christians, citing them as responsible for the new change in leadership. As a person in recovery, Harris has had to re-evaluate her own connection to faith and find strength in a higher power \(“Though he’s not necessarily a blue-eyed Jesus,” she laughs\), though she certainly knows what it’s like to “be told how to vote” in a Southern church setting. 

It was from the intersection of these social, personal, and political currents the album was born. And while much of the material on Boomerang Town was inspired by personal experience, the songs on this collection are far from autobiographical xeroxed copies. More than anything, they come from a place of emotional truth.

Boomerang Town traces the fortunes of a host of characters who live on the knife’s edge between hope and despair. The title track, whose sound recalls the best of Mary Chapin Carpenter’s ’90s work, features a young couple from a small-town working dead-end jobs who get “knocked up” and have their dreams put on hold. It is a portrait of rural desperation and the restless search for salvation against long odds. “This is what it’s like to be a part of the post- “‘Born To Run’ Generation,” Harris quips. “Springsteen’s generation had somewhere to run to. I’m not so sure mine does.” For the characters in these songs, escape isn’t always a matter of geographical distance.

“I tried a lot of perspectives \[on this one\],” Harris says about writing the title track. “My parents are high-school sweethearts and I was an accident and they’re still happily married. I worked at Wal-Mart when I was 19. I reflected on this guy who was the brother of a good friend of mine. He didn’t drop out. He knocked up his girlfriend and went into the military. Certainly \[the song\] is a combination of me and not me. It was me thinking about what might have gone differently for my parents, who are still in Waco and own a business there.” 

Harris’s father, whom she counts as a big supporter and responsible for much of her musical education, took her to the first Austin City Limits Music Festival, where she had the life-changing, Eureka moment of seeing Emmylou Harris, Patty Griffin, and Buddy and Julie Miller perform on stage at the same time. It was then the young Harris knew what she had to do. She had found her ticket out. 

Harris continues: “Why was I able to get out of my boomerang town? Why are others stuck there, longing to leave but unable to find their way out? Writing these songs, bringing these narrators to life, brought me closer to the answers,” she says.

Themes of grief and addiction permeate other sections of the record. “How Could You Be Gone,” which Harris wrote with her partner, the venerable folk songwriter Mary Gauthier, reflects on the passing of a close friend during the pandemic, as well as the 2017 death of Harris’s mentor and compadre Jimmy LaFave, a long-time fixture on the Americana scene who succumbed to cancer. “It’s been my experience that grief operates on its own timeline,” Harris says. “I wanted this track to build and repeat with intensity to mirror the experience of relentless grief.” Another song, “Fall \(Devin’s Song\),” is about a former childhood classmate of Harris’s who was accidentally shot and killed in the sixth grade. The song was inspired by a series of “In Memoriam” pieces the boy’s mother wrote to the local paper, and the song serves as a tribute to both of them, as well as a commentary on the timeless nature of grief. 

One of the album’s standout tracks is the lilting, Irish-influenced “The Fair And Dark Haired Lad,” a Chicks type-number that grapples with the seductive nature of alcohol. Another tune that deals with the demon rum, “Sam’s,” is far more dirge-like, and its dark, circular melody mirrors the claustrophobia and sense of trapping that comes with the onset of addiction and mental collapse. 

Boomerang Town is not entirely a lament, however, with songs like “Love is Gonna Come Again” and the wistful “Missing Someone” shining with hope in the face of the darkness. For this is a record that understands that love and grief are two sides of the same coin. It also announces the arrival of a great new songwriter on the scene. 

“My goal is to just write the best possible song I can write,” Harris says, “and I wanted to have ten songs that made sense together sonically. I still believe in the album format, and I wanted to lay the groundwork as a solid songwriter.” On Boomerang Town, Jaimee Harris, who was able to find her way out — unlike so many others — has accomplished all that, and much more.

title: Callie Watts
description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. description:
A "Rutas y Aventuras" program by Jack London Park Partners and " Senderos Naturales" by the Sonoma Ecology Center.

In the spring, this park comes alive with a multitude of bird species arriving to build their nests and forage for food—ranging from swallows and hummingbirds to hawks and owls. Come discover the wonderful birds found in the Sonoma Valley!

This workshop will focus on:

• How to use Merlin Bird ID to identify birds by song and photograph

• Basic tips for observing nature and improving your identification skills

• General information about common birds, plants, and animals found within the Sonoma Valley and Sonoma County

• How these apps help scientists and parks protect local biodiversity

This program is ideal for beginners, families, nature lovers, and anyone with a curious mind. No prior experience is required. We will proceed step-by-step, and there will be ample time for questions and guided practice.  This is an easy hike with a moderate incline.

title: What About Age? Art Exhibit
description:
*What About Age?* art exhibit has arrived in Marin County! Originally displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows, this exhibit explores ageism through contemporary art, featuring works by both local youth and senior artists.

*What About Age?* is an art exhibit and educational initiative designed to challenge stereotypes about aging, address ageism and social isolation, and promote intergenerational dialogue through the lens of art.

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

Katy's paintings are an exploration of light—how it shapes form, reveals color, and defines what we see.

description:

$275 – Registration Cost $25 – Materials Fee $300 – Total Registration CostIn this six-week course, participants will learn a unique approach to watercolor, intended to alleviate the frustration that many experience when learning this beautiful yet challenging medium.

About the Class

In this six-week course, participants will learn a unique approach to watercolor, intended to alleviate the frustration that many experience when learning this beautiful yet challenging medium. We will focus on strengthening one’s observational drawing skills, giving the artist a foundation off of which to build their paintings in a step-by-step layering process that trains the artist to see value and color. Our subject matter will be flora and fauna – a sampling of plants and animals. These subjects are great for beginners and experienced artists alike; their organic shapes make them forgiving drawing subjects, but their beauty can be a muse for life.  Instructor Hannah Day is a passionate nature lover and watercolorist and will share her unique approach to rendering botanicals and animal portraits in watercolor. This class will work both from photographs and from life, practicing observational drawing in addition to watercolor technique. With six class sessions, participants will have the opportunity to develop their skills and build muscle memory with a medium that often feels like it has a mind of its own.  This class is open to artists of all skill levels. All materials are provided.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Small Wonders
description:
Call for Art: Small Wonders

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

\- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

\- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

\- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed (144 sq in) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

\- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired (no alligator clips). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

\- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

title: Seth Kaminsky
description:
Seth Kaminsky is an alternative pop singer-songwriter/looping artist who will stop at nothing to build a career with his original music. Originally from the outskirts of Savannah, Georgia he currently resides in Sacramento, California where he continues to hone his ability as songwriter and performer. 

 

As an independent artist, Seth creates from a personal place but strives to share his music in a way that is unique, encouraging, relatable, and entertaining. 

 

Outside of performing and writing his original songs, you can often find Seth playing background music at various breweries, wineries, and miscellaneous events. Teaching private drum lessons. Continuing to spread his name via YouTube and other social media platforms. Drinking lots of coffee. And hanging out/going on adventures with his wife, Sierra. 

 

Seth is an extremely passionate and driven individual, determined to see his music go places. Currently he is in studio working on new music, has a single dropping August 5th and will be going on tour toward the end of August.

Trivia rounds feature a fun mix of wine-themed questions and unexpected topics, keeping the competition lighthearted and engaging. Guests may enjoy St. Francis wines available by the glass, along with a complimentary grazing table of seasonal bites. With prizes, plenty of laughs, and a welcoming vibe, Sip & Solve offers a playful way to experience the winery. Offered seasonally throughout the year, reservations are strongly recommended.

title: Fireside Chat with Sally Kohn - No Hate
description: A fireside chat with Sally Kohn and Martin Gobbee- Moderator.   Sally a member of the queer community, is a nationally recognized television commentator, writer and executive presence coac working iwth top executives and political leaders.  With her missage of connection and compassion for all, Sally is an in-demand speaker worldwide. In fun and informative talks, filled with powerful personal stories and mind-blowing research, Sally helps teams and communities move past conflict to find their common ground.  She leaves audiences feeling more empowered, hopeful and inspired.  Sally's first book, THE OPPOSITE OF HATE was published in April 2018.  She has three TED talks that have been viewed more than 6 million times. Moderator Martin Gobbee is a local business Manager in hospitality, and a member of the Wake UP Sonoma Board. He and Sally have been friends for many years, and the two are having a reunion on stage with this fireside chat.  He has a BA in history and a Master of Fine arts in acting from Brandeis University.

title: Inspire Napa Valley Event Support Alzheimer’s and Dementia Research
description:
The seventh annual Inspire Napa Valley will take place from Friday, April 24 – Sunday, April 26 in Napa Valley. Hosted by Kerrin Laz, founder of K. LAZ WINE COLLECTION, the wine community and beyond to raise funds and awareness to advance Alzheimer’s and dementia research nationally and enhance local care and support services for impacted families. Since its inception in 2017, the event has raised over $9 million for these vital efforts. This impactful event continues to unite wine industry leaders and enthusiasts to raise awareness, spark change, and secure national funding for an incredible cause. Don't miss out on this inspiring weekend that combines the best of Napa Valley with a commitment to making a difference!Events include:

Friday, April 24 | VIP Welcome Dinner – The Best of Oakville

5:30 PM | Gamble Estates, Oakville, CA

An exclusive evening, The Best of Oakville, brings together eight of the region’s best wineries as co-hosts, sharing their stories and wines, from rare library selections to current releases. The experience is paired with a wine country feast led by Napa Valley’s own Chef Sean Massey and joined in the kitchen by some of wine country’s leading vintners, winemakers, growers, and industry icons. This intimate gathering captures the spirit of true wine country hospitality.

The wineries include Dalla Valle Vineyards, Gamble Estates, Harlan Estate, Opus On, Screaming Eagle, Tench Vineyards, VHR – Vine Hill Ranch, FUTO

Saturday, April 25 | VIP Alzheimer’s Research Update & Wine Tasting Seminar: Deep Dive Into Oakville’s Best

10 AM | The Culinary Institute of America at Greystone, St. Helena, CA

Following an Alzheimer’s and dementia research update from Inspire Napa Valley’s Scientific Advisors, including Gates Ventures’ Senior Director of Health & Life Sciences, Farhad Imam, guests will enjoy an in-depth exploration of six of Oakville’s most exceptional wines, led by a distinguished panel including Antonio Galloni, founder of Vinous, and Ray Isle, Executive Wine Editor of Food & Wine.

Included for VIP guests. A limited number of seats are available for main event guests.

Saturday, April 25 | Grand Wine Tasting, Reception, Dinner & Auction

5 PM | Louis Martini Winery, St. Helena, CA

Enjoy the walk-around Grand Tasting featuring more than 35 of California’s most iconic wineries, alongside a selection of exciting rising star producers, followed by a festive wine country dinner and Inspire Napa Valley’s signature live auction and paddle raise.

Sunday, April 26 | VIP Farewell Brunch

10 AM | Ad Hoc + Addendum Garden

A farewell brunch featuring Chef Thomas Keller’s Ad Hoc fried chicken and waffles, alongside Bouchon seasonal dishes and a classic bloody mary and mimosa bar.

Express yourself with sharper footwork and styling.

title: Bella Rayne Band
description:
MEET BELLA RAYNE | GUITARIST

18 year old Bella Rayne is a self-taught guitarist, vocalist, and songwriter, born in the mountains of North Carolina and raised in coastal Mendocino, California, whose bold blend of jam band energy, Southern-tinged rock, ’90s grunge grit, and psychedelic spirit is rapidly capturing attention across the U.S. 

Her journey began during the pandemic, when boredom led her to resurrect an old Stratocaster she found in her garage. She fixed it up, learned to play by ear, and quickly found her voice — melding influences from rock, Americana, bluegrass, and the jam-band legacy into something deeply her own.                                              

Despite her young age, Bella has already shared the stage with seasoned artists and respected bands. Appearances alongside Allman Betts Family Revival, Melvin Seals & JGB, ALO, Jackie Greene, Oteil Burbridge, and members of Terrapin Family have all added to her early résumé PLUS she was touted as “one to watch” by her idol, Susan Tedeschi in Guitar World Magazine.

One of the most iconic moments of her rising career: she was entrusted to play the legendary guitar known as “Alligator” — once wielded by Jerry Garcia. That honor, courtesy of Grateful Guitars Foundation, has become a defining chapter in Bella’s journey. 

Bella has formed her own project, Bella Rayne Band — a high-energy, guitar-driven ensemble featuring a young lineup of seasoned musicians. Their sets are a blend of soulful Southern-rock, modern Americana and Grateful Dead reinterpretations plus their own originals, earning increasing demand across venues and festivals.

About the Class

This workshop is an introduction to mid-range soda firing, with hands-on training in the process of loading, firing, and maintaining our crossdraft kiln named “Julia”. Participants in this workshop will learn the fundamentals of atmospheric soda firing. The class will be instructed in the safety and care of the equipment as well as guided through the firing process. This workshop includes instruction on glazing, wadding the ceramic pieces, loading the kiln, firing the kiln, and kiln maintenance. Demos and Lectures will also happen during the firing. Participants will bring bisque-ware to be fired as bare clay or with slipped surfaces. There will be an assortment of flashing slips and glazes to apply to the bisqueware on loading day for those who choose to use them.  Each participant gets 1 cubic foot of firing space. \(Tip; Make sure all your pots fit approximately into a milk crate which is 1 cubic foot of space\). This firing will be a reduction fired cone 6 with sprayed soda at the end.

The following is a list of possible routes specifically selected for this hiking series: 

1) Sat 3/7 — Creekside + Waterfall loop, 3.6 miles, 750 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 2) Sat 3/14 – Vista Trail loop, 3.4 miles, 830 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 3) Sat 3/21 – Goodspeed to Nattkemper bench, 3.8 miles, 1,240 ft elevation \[meet @ Goodspeed lot\] 4) Sat 3/28 – Hillside to Neptune table + Meadow, 4.4 miles, 970 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 5) Sat 4/4 – Hillside + Vista Trail loop, 3.6 miles, 1,070 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 6) Sat 4/11 – False Lake Meadow & Lake Ilsanjo loop in Trionne-Annadel SP, 6.1 miles, 670 ft elevation \[meet @ Annadel's Cobblestone Trailhead\] 7) Sat 4/18 – Fern Lake + Orchard loop in SDC/Jack London SHP, 5.5 miles, 1,460 ft elevation \[meet @ Walnut & North St inside SDC; park on Grove St\] 8) Sat 4/25 – Bald Mtn summit (w/optional Headwaters detour, 5.8 miles), 5.1 miles, 1,670 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\]

Please note these routes are subject to change based on the group and weather. Wear appropriate footwear for rocky or slippery trails, and layers. Bring water, and if desired, a snack. The group will be limited to 35 participants. 

The hiking series costs $80 (plus a $10 parking fee per visit. Note that the Sugarloaf Annual Pass is $59 and valid at Sugarloaf and Jack London SHP), or free-of-cost for participants with a January 2025 or newer Park Rx from a Sonoma County Medical Provider.  The number of available Park Rx tickets is limited; please have your Rx ready at the time of sign up.

**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan. 

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

title: Calming the Restless Mind
description:
with Howard Cohn

Everyone wants to be calm and peaceful. Restlessness and agitation can arise when the mind is unsettled, the heart is reactive, and our perception of the present moment is unclear. During this day together, we will explore ways of steadying the heart and mind so that calm in the present moment becomes more accessible, insight develops naturally, and the heart softens.

During this daylong, we will draw on the Four Foundations of Mindfulness—being mindful of and sensitive to our bodies—beginning with the sensations of breathing, and expanding to include other physical sensations. We will explore how to feel pleasure more fully without trying to make it last, and how to more easily accommodate unpleasant experiences without becoming overwhelmed or reactive. We will also practice recognizing and working with our emotions, while learning how to relate to our thoughts more kindly and skillfully rather than being so easily carried away by them.

title: Inspire Napa Valley Event Support Alzheimer’s and Dementia Research
description:
The seventh annual Inspire Napa Valley will take place from Friday, April 24 – Sunday, April 26 in Napa Valley. Hosted by Kerrin Laz, founder of K. LAZ WINE COLLECTION, the wine community and beyond to raise funds and awareness to advance Alzheimer’s and dementia research nationally and enhance local care and support services for impacted families. Since its inception in 2017, the event has raised over $9 million for these vital efforts. This impactful event continues to unite wine industry leaders and enthusiasts to raise awareness, spark change, and secure national funding for an incredible cause. Don't miss out on this inspiring weekend that combines the best of Napa Valley with a commitment to making a difference!Events include:

Friday, April 24 | VIP Welcome Dinner – The Best of Oakville

5:30 PM | Gamble Estates, Oakville, CA

An exclusive evening, The Best of Oakville, brings together eight of the region’s best wineries as co-hosts, sharing their stories and wines, from rare library selections to current releases. The experience is paired with a wine country feast led by Napa Valley’s own Chef Sean Massey and joined in the kitchen by some of wine country’s leading vintners, winemakers, growers, and industry icons. This intimate gathering captures the spirit of true wine country hospitality.

The wineries include Dalla Valle Vineyards, Gamble Estates, Harlan Estate, Opus On, Screaming Eagle, Tench Vineyards, VHR – Vine Hill Ranch, FUTO

Saturday, April 25 | VIP Alzheimer’s Research Update & Wine Tasting Seminar: Deep Dive Into Oakville’s Best

10 AM | The Culinary Institute of America at Greystone, St. Helena, CA

Following an Alzheimer’s and dementia research update from Inspire Napa Valley’s Scientific Advisors, including Gates Ventures’ Senior Director of Health & Life Sciences, Farhad Imam, guests will enjoy an in-depth exploration of six of Oakville’s most exceptional wines, led by a distinguished panel including Antonio Galloni, founder of Vinous, and Ray Isle, Executive Wine Editor of Food & Wine.

Included for VIP guests. A limited number of seats are available for main event guests.

Saturday, April 25 | Grand Wine Tasting, Reception, Dinner & Auction

5 PM | Louis Martini Winery, St. Helena, CA

Enjoy the walk-around Grand Tasting featuring more than 35 of California’s most iconic wineries, alongside a selection of exciting rising star producers, followed by a festive wine country dinner and Inspire Napa Valley’s signature live auction and paddle raise.

Sunday, April 26 | VIP Farewell Brunch

10 AM | Ad Hoc + Addendum Garden

A farewell brunch featuring Chef Thomas Keller’s Ad Hoc fried chicken and waffles, alongside Bouchon seasonal dishes and a classic bloody mary and mimosa bar.

title: INTO THE LIGHT: Light-filled aintings by Katy Boggs
description:
Katy's paintings are an exploration of light—how it shapes form, reveals color, and defines what we see.

"I am drawn to moments where light is felt as much as seen: filtering through dense leaves, towering in the crowns of trees, glinting off cresting waves, or softening into the quiet glow of a sunset. Light is everywhere; without it, there is no seeing. Beyond its physical presence, it also carries a deeper resonance as a symbol of hope. In a time of uncertainty, this work seeks to bring light into the image, both visually and metaphorically."

Reception: April 25, 4 to 6 pm.

title: "We The Sculptors…International Sculpture Days
description:
From ancient monuments carved in stone to bold contemporary abstraction, sculpture has always been a defiant presence in the world. It occupies space and refuses to be ignored.

This year’s International Sculpture Days event embraces the belief that sculpture can inspire, provoke, and challenge the world around us. Each artist will present their work , and visitors can engage in acts of “defiant dissidence,” exploring how art can serve as both personal reflection and public voice.

The event draws on a long tradition of artists and citizens using visual language to express dissent, question norms, and imagine new possibilities. At its core, *We The Sculptors* affirms the enduring role of artists to challenge, to question, and to stand visibly in the public square.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net**

title: Calistoga Unwind Weekend
description: Classic Chrome | Bathrobe Chic Join us for Unwind Weekend!  For more than 150 years, Calistoga has been a place where people come to slow down, soak, sip, and truly unwind. From natural hot springs and mud baths to long afternoons in tasting rooms and strolls through our historic downtown, relaxation isn’t a trend here; it’s our heritage. Unwind Weekend celebrates that spirit in the most Calistoga way possible: playful, elevated, and effortlessly charming. Saturday kicks off with a Classic Car Show on Cedar Street — vintage style, community energy, and a nod to timeless California cool. And as evening settles in, the Bathrobe Bar Crawl invites guests to do what Calistoga has always done best: slip into something comfortable and enjoy great food, great drinks, and great company. This isn’t just a series of events. It’s a weekend designed around staying, playing, and unwinding in Napa Valley’s original wellness destination.

title: Classic Chrome | Unwind Weekend Event
description: The Classic Car Show of Calistoga is a beloved community tradition and a highlight of Unwind Weekend. Set in the heart of downtown Calistoga, the show celebrates the timeless beauty and craftsmanship of classic automobiles manufactured prior to 1980. Stroll among rows of meticulously maintained vintage vehicles, meet the proud owners, and soak in the relaxed Napa Valley atmosphere. Local food and beverage options will be available nearby, or bring a picnic, settle in, and enjoy an afternoon surrounded by chrome, curves, and nostalgia. Cars are not formally judged, though informal People’s Choice recognition may add to the fun. If you are the proud owner of a classic car, we invite you to submit your application and be part of this special weekend. The show is open to the public, and admission is free.

title: Small Wonders
description:
Call for Art: Small Wonders

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

\- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

\- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

\- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed (144 sq in) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

\- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired (no alligator clips). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

\- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

Key Dates:

\- Entry Deadline: May 10, 2026 (9 PM)

\- Notification of Selection: By May 13, 2026

\- Shipped Work Deadline: Wednesday, May 27, 2026 (must include pre-paid return label)

\- Hand-Delivery: Sunday, May 31 (12–4 PM) and Monday, June 1 (11 AM–1 PM)

\- Exhibition Dates: June 4, 2026 – July 19, 2026

\- Opening Reception: Saturday, June 6, 2026 (4–6 PM)

\- Pick-up/Return Shipping: July 19 (12–4 PM) and July 20 (11 AM–1 PM); shipping the week of July 20.

Entry Fees:

\- Non-Members: $50 (1 entry), $55 (2 entries), $60 (3 entries). Includes a $60 yearly supporter membership.

\- Current Members: $40 (1 entry), $45 (2 entries), $50 (3 entries).

title: Por la Luz de la Luna: A Mexican Ballet
description: This original ballet libretto was inspired by award-winning author and arts activist Aida Salazar's story of her great-aunt, Jovita Valdovinos, who fought for religious freedom in Mexico's Cristero War in the 1930s.Por la Luz de la Lunabrings a fictional account of Jovita's story to life, weaving history, mythology, and family legacy into a powerful theatrical experience while celebrating her heroism. As one of the few Mexican-themed ballets in history, it creates a space for dancers of all backgrounds to portray Latina/o characters, highlighting unique stories and honoring Mexican and Mexican-American heritage on stage. Set to 20th-century Mexican classical music by composers such as Carlos Chávez and José Pablo Moncayo, the ballet is brought to life through striking sets and Aztec-inspired costumes designed by visual artist PEMEX. It premiered on April 9, 2016, at the Sebastiani Theatre and continues to be a highlight of the company's repertory.

title: Self-Defense
description:
Are you prepared to face the unexpected? Join us for self-defense class

In a world that demands alertness, knowing how to protect yourself is not a luxury—it’s a necessity. Join our intensive 2 HOURS Self-Defense class lesson \(\+ stay extra hour if you want to just practice\) class designed to give you the fundamental tools, techniques, and mindset needed for immediate safety.

This highly condensed course focuses on awareness, prevention, and simple, effective physical responses you can rely on when seconds count. We prioritize getting you to safety above all else.

Workshop Details

The “Airway Priority”: technique to instantly break front and rear chokes, ensuring you can breathe and think clearly under pressure.

Clothing & Control: Discover how to use an attacker’s grip against them. We’ll cover shirt and lapel grabs, teaching you how to use leverage to break their “frame” and create distance.

Asset Defense \(Backpacks & Purses\): Most thefts involve a grab of your gear. We’ll practice how to defend against being dragged by a strap, when to “shed the load,” and how to use your bag as a temporary shield.

Counter-Striking Foundations: Learn to use “biological tools”—palm strikes, knees, and elbows—to disrupt an attacker’s focus so you can facilitate your release.

Important Details

Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our floors in great condition.

2 HOURS Self-Defense class lesson \(\+ stay extra hour if you want to just practice\)

Date: April 25, 2026

TIME: 1:00 PM – 3:00 PM \(\+ extra practice if you want to stay until 4:00 PM\)

title: Javier Zamora in Conversation with Albert Flynn DeSilver
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center, in partnership with Canal Alliance and Book Passage, is proud to present an evening with acclaimed poet and author Javier Zamora, in conversation with poet, memoirist, and educator Albert Flynn DeSilver, on Saturday, April 25 from 6 – 7:30PM at the San Geronimo Valley Community Center.

Javier Zamora is widely celebrated for his powerful, intimate writing that explores migration, identity, and belonging. Born in El Salvador, Zamora came to the United States by himself at the age of nine and later lived in the Canal District of San Rafael—an experience that profoundly shapes his work. His bestselling memoir, Solito, and his poetry have resonated with readers nationwide for their lyrical language and deeply human storytelling.

In this special event, Zamora will be interviewed by Albert Flynn DeSilver, known for his dynamic presence and thoughtful, wide-ranging conversations that invite both literary insight and personal reflection. Together, they will explore Zamora’s creative process, lived experience, and the themes that animate his work.

A Special Pre-Event Reception

We warmly invite you to upgrade for a special pre-event experience, from 5:00–6:00pm, which includes:

A signed copy of Solito

Exclusive time with Javier Zamora

Light bites and festive beverages

The opportunity to connect with senior leaders from Canal Alliance and SGVCC, along with fellow supporters

This experience is designed to bring you closer to the people, stories, and relationships that make this work possible — and to celebrate the power of community-centered storytelling. Please be sure to choose the “Pre-Event Reception” option at check out.

This event is presented by Canal Alliance, the San Geronimo Valley Community Center and Book Passage, organizations united by a shared commitment to literacy, community, and cultural exchange

Simultaneous English to Spanish interpretation will be provided.

Javier Zamora es reconocido por su escritura poderosa e íntima que explora la migración, la identidad y el sentido de pertenencia. Nacido en El Salvador, Zamora llegó a los Estados Unidos solo, a los nueve años, y vivió en el vecindario del Canal de San Rafael — experiencias que marcan su poesía y su exitoso libro, Solito. En este evento especial, Zamora será entrevistado por Albert Flynn DeSilver; juntos explorarán su proceso creativo, su experiencia de vida y los temas que dan forma a su obra.

title: SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River
description:
Slow down and float into a quieter rhythm with SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River at The Floathouse Petaluma. Launching from downtown Petaluma, this peaceful on-the-water yoga experience feels worlds away from the bustle—set in the calm, protected turning basin where the river naturally invites you to relax.

This all-levels, 90-minute session welcomes everyone, from first-time paddle boarders and yoga newcomers to experienced practitioners. We begin with a short, gentle paddle from the docks to get comfortable on your board \(knees are always welcome\), then anchor together so tidal movement won’t interrupt your flow. Once settled, you’re free to move, stretch, rest, or simply be—guided by expert instruction and supported by the shared energy of the group. Evening sessions and morning sessions allow YOU to choose the vibe that suits you best.

All equipment is provided, including extra-stable paddleboards that are wider and longer than a yoga mat, designed to help you feel grounded and secure on the water.

Perfect for locals and Bay Area visitors alike, SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River offers a rare chance to experience downtown Petaluma from the water—peaceful, playful, and deeply restorative.

It’s YOUR river. Come out and play.

title: Clear Horizons: Works by Peter Hassen
description: After more than three decades as a working artist in Sonoma and across the North Bay, Peter Hassen will mark the end of a chapter with a special two-day studio event, Clear Horizons: Works by Peter Hassen, April 25-26 from 10 AM to 4 PM at his White Barn Studio \(900 Petaluma Ave., Sonoma\). Known for his sculptural work and public art projects-including installations on Sonoma Plaza and participation in the Napa Art Walk-Hassen has been an active part of the region's creative community. As he prepares to relocate to Spain, the event offers collectors and the broader arts community a rare opportunity to view a wide selection of works from throughout his career.

title: Cultivating a Wise and Kind Heart
description:
We invite you to spend a day on the land, resting in the Buddha’s teachings on wisdom and kindness. Together, we will practice cultivating kind awareness that supports us in growing our capacity to meet the joys and challenges of being human. As we learn to steadily meet things as they are, the wisdom of the Dhamma unfolds, and through this cultivation we touch into the possibility of freedom.

The day will include guided sitting and Dhamma reflections and opportunity for walking meditations. The day will be held mostly in silence, with a few intentional moments for community connection and shared reflection.

title: Edible & Medicinal Plant Walk
description:
Weaving in natural history, ethnobotany, herbalism and folktales, this walk will open your senses, as well as your curiosity to the abundance of plantlore in Sonoma County.

Tickets are $15 for adults, $7.5 for youth (12-17 year olds; all children under 18 must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian), students, Sugarloaf members, and Sugarloaf or RFO volunteers, and free for children under 12. Meet at the White Barn parking lot. Bring at least a quart of water and a lunch and be prepared for a leisurely 2-3 mile walk with a 250-ft climb. Wear layers, appropriate footwear for slippery (and possibly muddy) terrain, and sun protection. Heavy rains cancel; parking fees apply.

Edible plant information is for educational purposes only. Foraging is illegal in CA State Parks.

title: Inspire Napa Valley Event Support Alzheimer’s and Dementia Research
description:
The seventh annual Inspire Napa Valley will take place from Friday, April 24 – Sunday, April 26 in Napa Valley. Hosted by Kerrin Laz, founder of K. LAZ WINE COLLECTION, the wine community and beyond to raise funds and awareness to advance Alzheimer’s and dementia research nationally and enhance local care and support services for impacted families. Since its inception in 2017, the event has raised over $9 million for these vital efforts. This impactful event continues to unite wine industry leaders and enthusiasts to raise awareness, spark change, and secure national funding for an incredible cause. Don't miss out on this inspiring weekend that combines the best of Napa Valley with a commitment to making a difference!Events include:

Friday, April 24 | VIP Welcome Dinner – The Best of Oakville

5:30 PM | Gamble Estates, Oakville, CA

An exclusive evening, The Best of Oakville, brings together eight of the region’s best wineries as co-hosts, sharing their stories and wines, from rare library selections to current releases. The experience is paired with a wine country feast led by Napa Valley’s own Chef Sean Massey and joined in the kitchen by some of wine country’s leading vintners, winemakers, growers, and industry icons. This intimate gathering captures the spirit of true wine country hospitality.

The wineries include Dalla Valle Vineyards, Gamble Estates, Harlan Estate, Opus On, Screaming Eagle, Tench Vineyards, VHR – Vine Hill Ranch, FUTO

Saturday, April 25 | VIP Alzheimer’s Research Update & Wine Tasting Seminar: Deep Dive Into Oakville’s Best

Following an Alzheimer’s and dementia research update from Inspire Napa Valley’s Scientific Advisors, including Gates Ventures’ Senior Director of Health & Life Sciences, Farhad Imam, guests will enjoy an in-depth exploration of six of Oakville’s most exceptional wines, led by a distinguished panel including Antonio Galloni, founder of Vinous, and Ray Isle, Executive Wine Editor of Food & Wine.

Included for VIP guests. A limited number of seats are available for main event guests.

Saturday, April 25 | Grand Wine Tasting, Reception, Dinner & Auction

5 PM | Louis Martini Winery, St. Helena, CA

Enjoy the walk-around Grand Tasting featuring more than 35 of California’s most iconic wineries, alongside a selection of exciting rising star producers, followed by a festive wine country dinner and Inspire Napa Valley’s signature live auction and paddle raise.

Sunday, April 26 | VIP Farewell Brunch

10 AM | Ad Hoc + Addendum Garden

title: INTO THE LIGHT: Light-filled aintings by Katy Boggs
description:
Katy's paintings are an exploration of light—how it shapes form, reveals color, and defines what we see.

"I am drawn to moments where light is felt as much as seen: filtering through dense leaves, towering in the crowns of trees, glinting off cresting waves, or softening into the quiet glow of a sunset. Light is everywhere; without it, there is no seeing. Beyond its physical presence, it also carries a deeper resonance as a symbol of hope. In a time of uncertainty, this work seeks to bring light into the image, both visually and metaphorically."

Reception: April 25, 4 to 6 pm.

About the Class

This workshop is an introduction to mid-range soda firing, with hands-on training in the process of loading, firing, and maintaining our crossdraft kiln named “Julia”. Participants in this workshop will learn the fundamentals of atmospheric soda firing. The class will be instructed in the safety and care of the equipment as well as guided through the firing process. This workshop includes instruction on glazing, wadding the ceramic pieces, loading the kiln, firing the kiln, and kiln maintenance. Demos and Lectures will also happen during the firing. Participants will bring bisque-ware to be fired as bare clay or with slipped surfaces. There will be an assortment of flashing slips and glazes to apply to the bisqueware on loading day for those who choose to use them.  Each participant gets 1 cubic foot of firing space. \(Tip; Make sure all your pots fit approximately into a milk crate which is 1 cubic foot of space\). This firing will be a reduction fired cone 6 with sprayed soda at the end.

title: Wood Engraving - 2 Day Intensive Workshop
description:
This two-day workshop introduces the art and practice of wood engraving. The hard woods used to make wood engraving blocks are type-high (.918”, the height of metal type) and are cut across the grain rather than parallel to it like wood cuts. These durable end-grain blocks allow for extensive detail. The tools used are gravers (or burins) that are different than the gouge tools used for wood cuts. This versatile form of printmaking requires little space and minimal equipment and is perfect for a small home studio.

Day 1: We will start with a brief history of wood engraving including its long relationship to letterpress printing, and we will study examples of period and contemporary wood engravings. Students will begin with a sampler block to explore the effects of various tools, proof the block on the press, and transfer a design onto another block to consider the approach for their first engraving.

Day 2: Students will learn how to sharpen their gravers and continue to engrave their blocks. We will become familiar with basic use of the Vandercook SP-15 cylinder press to ink and proof the block and troubleshoot issues when printing. Printing an edition of a block will be discussed, and those wanting to contribute a print to the workshop portfolio are encouraged to do so. Students will leave the workshop with the skills to master the graver tool to create intricate prints, a value test block for future reference, an instructive handout, a block to edition, and a portfolio of workshop prints.

Level: Beginner – no previous experience necessary

*Includes $50 materials fee, which covers #3 elliptical tint tool and two 3”x 4” end-grain maple blocks)*

**INSTRUCTOR**

**Colleen Dwire** initially learned wood engraving in a workshop with American Master John DePol and has been practicing for over thirty years. She exhibits her prints internationally. Colleen is an elected member of the Society of Wood Engravers (UK) and serves as Secretary and Exhibitions Officer for Wood Engravers’ Network (USA) and as a board member of North Bay Letterpress Arts. Learn more at www.colleendwire.com and follow on colleendwire.bsky.social.

Whether you’re a seasoned pro or have two left feet, come sweat, smile, and discover your new favorite beat.

Who: All adult ages and skill levels.

When: Sundays @ 10:00 AM.

The Vibe: Pure fun, global rhythms, and a community that moves together.

About Zeena

Zeena Quinn’s World Dance classes are based on learning coordination, motivating the brain, dance techniques, and therefore, mind-body transformation. By creating a supportive system, participants discover themselves in their own way via dance.

Participants will work upper and lower body, cardio and mostly rhythms & coordination. One will understand and learn to identify the different rhythms while having fun! Zeena has a lifetime of experience in dance, professional performance, choreography, teaching, as well as, in fitness and resistance training.

Zeena has toured the Bay Area presenting a variety of American swing, Charlston, hip hop, disco, line dances, and international dance styles such as Bollywood, Afro-Brazilian/Samba, Flamenco, and European and Eastern Folk. These authentic dance techniques demonstrate how our body is an instrument. Because of her extensive range of dance training, she brings the authenticity of technique into her vibrant teaching style.

Come take a trip around theworld! Comfortable clothes and worn shoes that tie. No Hoka or hiking shoes please.

title: "We The Sculptors…International Sculpture Days
description:
From ancient monuments carved in stone to bold contemporary abstraction, sculpture has always been a defiant presence in the world. It occupies space and refuses to be ignored.

This year’s International Sculpture Days event embraces the belief that sculpture can inspire, provoke, and challenge the world around us. Each artist will present their work , and visitors can engage in acts of “defiant dissidence,” exploring how art can serve as both personal reflection and public voice.

The event draws on a long tradition of artists and citizens using visual language to express dissent, question norms, and imagine new possibilities. At its core, *We The Sculptors* affirms the enduring role of artists to challenge, to question, and to stand visibly in the public square.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: GLYPH  - Art Exhibition
description:

Big news! Personal Space is back from our \(much needed\) hiatus. Join us next Sunday, March 15 \(2-5pm\) for the opening of  Glyph. This is our first opening since Village opened up next door, and it’s sure to be a party!

Featuring thirteen artists from the Bay Area and beyond, Glyph embraces a liminal space which allows subconscious connections to reign and centers gut feeling as a source of poetry, mystery, and magic. Collectively, these artists draw from an enigmatic lexicon of symbols, favoring inscrutable familiarity over anything known or quantified. This intuitive language manifests through a varied approach to material translation that underscores, and celebrates, our innate ability to understand things deeply without having to define them in words.

title: Small Wonders
description:
Call for Art: Small Wonders

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

\- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

\- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

\- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed (144 sq in) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

\- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired (no alligator clips). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

\- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

Key Dates:

\- Entry Deadline: May 10, 2026 (9 PM)

\- Notification of Selection: By May 13, 2026

\- Shipped Work Deadline: Wednesday, May 27, 2026 (must include pre-paid return label)

\- Hand-Delivery: Sunday, May 31 (12–4 PM) and Monday, June 1 (11 AM–1 PM)

\- Exhibition Dates: June 4, 2026 – July 19, 2026

\- Opening Reception: Saturday, June 6, 2026 (4–6 PM)

\- Pick-up/Return Shipping: July 19 (12–4 PM) and July 20 (11 AM–1 PM); shipping the week of July 20.

Entry Fees:

\- Non-Members: $50 (1 entry), $55 (2 entries), $60 (3 entries). Includes a $60 yearly supporter membership.

\- Current Members: $40 (1 entry), $45 (2 entries), $50 (3 entries).

title: Por la Luz de la Luna: A Mexican Ballet
description: This original ballet libretto was inspired by award-winning author and arts activist Aida Salazar's story of her great-aunt, Jovita Valdovinos, who fought for religious freedom in Mexico's Cristero War in the 1930s.Por la Luz de la Lunabrings a fictional account of Jovita's story to life, weaving history, mythology, and family legacy into a powerful theatrical experience while celebrating her heroism. As one of the few Mexican-themed ballets in history, it creates a space for dancers of all backgrounds to portray Latina/o characters, highlighting unique stories and honoring Mexican and Mexican-American heritage on stage. Set to 20th-century Mexican classical music by composers such as Carlos Chávez and José Pablo Moncayo, the ballet is brought to life through striking sets and Aztec-inspired costumes designed by visual artist PEMEX. It premiered on April 9, 2016, at the Sebastiani Theatre and continues to be a highlight of the company's repertory.

title: Old Wine, New Bottle
description:
What if Mozart’s music could surprise you with new colors you didn’t know you were missing? This program shines a spotlight on two of his favorite voices: the basset horn and the basset clarinet. Deeper, warmer, and more velvety than their modern descendants, these instruments were prized in Mozart’s time for their ability to sing, sigh, and whisper with uncanny intimacy.

The program begins with a charming quintet by Mozart’s contemporary Johann Backofen, whose writing shows off the basset horn’s mellow glow and conversational wit. Mozart’s youthful “Milanese” string quartet follows, sparkling with elegance and invention. The program culminates in Mozart’s beloved clarinet quintet, a work of timeless beauty, virtuosity, and ingenuity performed here on a replica of the original basset clarinet Mozart had in mind. Performed on period instruments, this concert offers a chance to hear familiar music scrubbed clean—lighter, more transparent, and irresistibly alive.

**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

title: Patron Saints of Influence Spring Reading & Open Mic
description:
The next Patron Saints of Influence quarterly literary reading & open mic on Sunday, April 26 will pay homage to the poet, musician, and political activist **Gil Scott-Heron** with featured readings by **Yume Kim**, **Steve Shain**, and **Grayson Thompson**. Find us at Shady Oak Barrel House in Santa Rosa starting at 4PM.

As always, you are also welcome to share some of your own written work in 5 minutes or less during the open mic (arrive early to sign up). That could include song lyrics or spoken word if you're especially inspired by Gil Scott-Heron, but all words are welcome as long as they're not hateful.

**About the Featured Readers:**

**Yume Kim** is a poet, educator, and author of *Reserve the Right*. In 2011, she moved from her home state Virginia to California for her graduate studies at San Francisco State University. There, she earned both an M.A. in English and an M.F.A. in Creative Writing. Additionally, she is a recipient of the following fellowships: Kundiman (June 2012), The Ruby Creatives in Residence (2022-2023), and The Bay Area Writing Project Invitational Summer Institute (June 2024). Some of her works can also be found in the following journals: *gesture*, *sPARKLE + bLINK*, *West Wind Review*, *Transfer*, S*ugared Water*, *Writing Without Walls*, *The Bangalore Review*, *You Might Need to Hear This*, and *The Sad Girls Lit Club*.

**Steve Shain**'s journey with the voice of the bass began in 1963 in Chicago Heights, Ill. Since being introduced to beat generation poet ruth weiss by painter Paul Beattie in 1984, Steve has usually been seen accompanying poets throughout the Bay Area. Most recently, Steve’s own verbiage is being shared; a unique/personal perspective on a life lived, from a survivor/observer/commentator. The voice of Steve’s bass is special, too: a 1930s Alcoa made in Buffalo, NY, Dura (the bass) speaks: not jazz/not classical/not bluegrass but “BASSICNESS” … inherent tones & rhythms dictated by inspiration and the present tense. His teachers include Florence Dangermond, Nancy McCain, Edward Krolick, Curtis Burris, and Glen Moore. His muse-ical mentors include Ron Crotty, Darrell DeVore, Richard Waters, and Harry Partch. He has also shared stages with ruth weiss, Jack Micheline, Lawrence Ferlinghetti, Eugene Ruggles, Sherrill Milnes, Eugene Istomin, Earl LeClaire, and David Best; and recorded with Leopard Set, Tom Waits, and others. When not playing bass, Steve can be found as proprietor of “bassic sewing”, a Santa Rosa leather fabrication & repair shop.

**Grayson Thompson** \[he/him\] is a Black, Jamaican-American, queer transgender cowboy poet who moonlights as a therapist. He is the inaugural Slam Poetry Champion of Santa Rosa, CA. A mouthful, Grayson is Foglifter Press' 2024 Start A Riot! Chapbook Prize Winner with *SAND BODIED FLORIDA BOY* and Winner of Write Bloody Publishing's 2024 Jack McCarthy Book Prize for his full-length collection, *A CONGREGATION OF ALLIGATORS* (September 2025). Born in Massachusetts, raised between Florida and New England, Grayson’s work centers the body and its relationship to the prerequisites needed for social existence…to be recognized by others as being human. His poems explore race, queerness, and gender; family, grief, and grace.

title: JaM Cellars Presents KT Tunstall with support from TOMI
description:
April 26, 2026
PURCHASE TICKETS HERE  
Doors 7pm/ Show 8pm
Ages: 12+ 
KT Tunstall has always lived in pursuit of creative evolution. The Grammy-nominated, Brit Award-winning Scottish artist made an indelible mark on the music world with her 2004 multi-platinum debut Eye to the Telescope, immediately establishing herself as a formidable force. 
Nearly two decades on, Tunstall’s career has spanned an eclectic array of genres – from introspective folk to blistering rock and experimental electro-pop – while she has remained one of the most iconic live performers of her generation, renowned for her extraordinary voice that shifts effortlessly from soulful to bluesy grit to delicate folk-pop. Her music embodies a balance of raw emotion and visceral energy, always remaining in constant service to memorable melody, while her live shows are punctuated by a warm and often hilarious rapport with her audience. 
Tunstall’s breakthrough came in 2004 on the revered UK music show Later… with Jools Holland. A last-minute addition to the lineup after rapper Nas dropped out, Tunstall took to the stage armed with just her guitar, a loop pedal, and a tambourine on the floor. “Do that new ‘Woo Hoo’ one,” her Label Boss suggested. So she did – and the rest, as they say, is history. Her stripped-back yet electrifying performance of “Black Horse and the Cherry Tree” captivated audiences instantly, propelling her to global fame. In a pre-loop-pedal revolution era, long before artists like Ed Sheeran popularized its use, Tunstall stood out as a trailblazer and true pioneer of its use, making the ‘one-woman-band’ setup not just novel but essential. 
“That night made me understand something important,” Tunstall recalls. “It’s not just about the song, it’s how you execute it under pressure, how you share it. I didn’t realise how much people would love seeing how I did it. I think people got a kick out of seeing someone do something risky live, and pull it off.” 
Her debut album, Eye to the Telescope, solidified her as a leading voice in the burgeoning folk-pop movement. Her debut record produced enduring hits such as the rhythmically charged “Black Horse and the Cherry Tree,” the tender ballad “Other Side of the World,” and the soaring anthem “Suddenly I See,” which would later become synonymous with The Devil Wears Prada. She recalls her Manager at the time saying to her, “enjoy this moment; they’ve used your entire unedited song for the beginning of the film, no dialogue. It’ll probably never happen like this again”. The iconic opening scene of the movie cemented her place in a defining cultural moment. 
Amid a crowded field of rising female singer-songwriters, Tunstall stood apart, exuding authenticity and displaying an unmistakable stage presence and musicianship. “There are two core elements to my style,” she reflects. “I’ve got the troubadour, acoustic, emotionally driven side, and then there’s the raw, fiery rock element with a ton of teeth.” This duality – switching from heartfelt acoustic ballads to gritty rock anthems – has been a hallmark of her career. 
By the time her sophomore album Drastic Fantastic was released in 2007, Tunstall had evolved from folk-pop ingénue to bona fide rock star. The record leaned further into guitar-driven rock without losing the melodic hooks that defined her sound. It reflected her resistance to being confined to one musical identity, pushing beyond her folk roots. This was further explored in her 2010 album Tiger Suit, recorded in Berlin, where she fused acoustic instrumentation with pulsing electronic beats, breaking new creative ground. 
Invisible Empire // Crescent Moon (2013) marked a dramatic shift in her sound and mood. Recorded in the widescreen desert landscapes of Tucson, Arizona, the album embraced a stripped-back, Americana-tinged aesthetic, mirroring a period of personal upheaval, including the loss of her father and the breakdown of her marriage. Critically lauded, the album revealed some of Tunstall’s most intimate and vulnerable work. 
As she entered the second decade of her career, Tunstall embarked on one of her most ambitious ventures yet: a trilogy of albums exploring the interwoven themes of soul, body, and mind. The first, 2016’s KIN, was the ‘soul’ record – a bright, anthemic return that rekindled her love of music after a period of disillusionment. 
In 2018, she followed with WAX, the ‘body’ record, which embraced her rock instincts with a visceral intensity. The trilogy concluded in 2022 with NUT, the ‘mind’ album, written during a period of profound life changes, including her move to the U.S., as well as creating an album remotely through the pandemic. “This trilogy represents probably the most extreme and transformative period of my life,” Tunstall reflects. 
Earlier this year, as the 20th anniversary of Eye to the Telescope approached, Tunstall was honored with the prestigious Ivor Novello Award for ‘Outstanding Song Collection’ – a testament to her enduring influence among both peers and fans alike. In the past year, she has toured both as a solo act and co-headliner with iconic U.S. singer-songwriter Shawn Colvin, while also serving as a special guest on tours with Roger Daltrey, and fellow Scots, Texas. 
In addition to her prolific music career, Tunstall has expanded into composing for film and theater. Most recently, it was announced that Clueless, The Musical, for which she composed the music, will make its West End debut in February 2025. 
Next year, Tunstall will celebrate the 20th anniversary of her seminal debut album Eye to the Telescope with a series of special performances and a re-release featuring additional tracks, including an inaugural headline show at London’s Royal Albert Hall. After two decades, KT Tunstall remains a vital, ever-evolving artist – one who continues to surprise, innovate, and captivate audiences around the world. 
TOMI 
Sometimes we have to leave everything behind in order to evolve. 
Songwriter/Producer Pam Autuori, who performs as TOMI (she/her), found herself on that journey a few years ago. 
On her upcoming album “Break It Til You Fix It” — produced by Autuori — she experiments with her dynamic vocal range and pushes the boundaries on self reflection and impulsivity. 
Learning towards her Americana roots, the lyrics are thoughtful and blend effortlessly with the production, making the listening experience a visual sonic landscape. 
TOMI’s style is characterized by ferocious guitar and resounding vocals — an unfettered, urgent, and emotionally supercharged sound that was forged from a ruthless determination to sing, play, and do things her own way, even in the face of life’s obstacles. 
Her new album “Break it Til You Fix it” comes out March 10, 2026. 
Check out her latest single Let Me Down about chasing someone you can’t catch.
