*What About Age?* art exhibit has arrived in Marin County! Originally displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows, this exhibit explores ageism through contemporary art, featuring works by both local youth and senior artists.

*What About Age?* is an art exhibit and educational initiative designed to challenge stereotypes about aging, address ageism and social isolation, and promote intergenerational dialogue through the lens of art.

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Small Wonders
description:
Call for Art: Small Wonders

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

\- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

\- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

\- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed (144 sq in) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

\- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired (no alligator clips). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

\- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

Key Dates:

\- Entry Deadline: May 10, 2026 (9 PM)

\- Notification of Selection: By May 13, 2026

\- Shipped Work Deadline: Wednesday, May 27, 2026 (must include pre-paid return label)

\- Hand-Delivery: Sunday, May 31 (12–4 PM) and Monday, June 1 (11 AM–1 PM)

\- Exhibition Dates: June 4, 2026 – July 19, 2026

\- Opening Reception: Saturday, June 6, 2026 (4–6 PM)

\- Pick-up/Return Shipping: July 19 (12–4 PM) and July 20 (11 AM–1 PM); shipping the week of July 20.

Entry Fees:

\- Non-Members: $50 (1 entry), $55 (2 entries), $60 (3 entries). Includes a $60 yearly supporter membership.

\- Current Members: $40 (1 entry), $45 (2 entries), $50 (3 entries).

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

\- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

\- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

\- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed (144 sq in) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

\- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired (no alligator clips). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

\- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

About the Class

This workshop is an introduction to mid-range soda firing, with hands-on training in the process of loading, firing, and maintaining our crossdraft kiln named “Julia”. Participants in this workshop will learn the fundamentals of atmospheric soda firing. The class will be instructed in the safety and care of the equipment as well as guided through the firing process. This workshop includes instruction on glazing, wadding the ceramic pieces, loading the kiln, firing the kiln, and kiln maintenance. Demos and Lectures will also happen during the firing. Participants will bring bisque-ware to be fired as bare clay or with slipped surfaces. There will be an assortment of flashing slips and glazes to apply to the bisqueware on loading day for those who choose to use them.  Each participant gets 1 cubic foot of firing space. \(Tip; Make sure all your pots fit approximately into a milk crate which is 1 cubic foot of space\). What you’ll do

What is printmaking? We invite you into our print studio to experience a fun beginner’s journey through this incredible art form in five paced weeks. Join Kelly in this unique introduction to print through the world of monotype, relief, intaglio and stencil screenprinting. This popular multi-session workshop is only taught twice per year in the spring and fall seasons. Students will try various techniques in this guided, hands-on class to create a beginning portfolio of prints. Learn a basic understanding of the four classic methods within the family of printmaking and gain access to our member’s print studio to continue working on your own projects. This class is perfect for absolute beginners or even experienced artists who may need a refresher course in printmaking. 

Monotype – Create a single print on a flat matrix using ink and a variety of marks and  textures

Relief – Carve, ink and block print using a mini speedy carve block and a linocut tool

Intaglio – Draw, scratch and ink onto a surface to roll out a creative print using a small press

Stencil – Pull a silkscreen and learn to transfer a flat stencil to make a colorful printed impression

No prior printmaking experience is necessary. This class requires hand dexterity to maneuver carving tools and studio equipment. Students must feel comfortable handling machinery.

title: Morning Yoga
description: Regenerative Ayurvedic Yoga with Tirza Dawn Come, step onto your mat with an open heart and an open mind. Invest in your self care and join us for morning yoga in the OCA studio. $20 per class, $15 for OCA members. Each Wednesday from 9:00-10:15 AM in our Studio. Pay at the door for a-la-carte sessions or use the links below to pay ahead for four weeks at a time.  Pay Online 4 sessions - OCA members  Pay Online 4 sessions - non members Tirza Dawn Naramore is a yogi, mother, artist, ceremonialist and lover of life. She has been practicing and teaching yoga and meditation for 30 years and offers yoga retreats and trainings that center on optimum health, self realization and self love. Her teachers are from many yoga and tantric traditions, but her primary lineages are Iyengar and Kali Ray.  Tirza is deeply devoted to community building and is honored to have created a number of community supported non profits including Mystic Family Circus and The AWAKEN Project, which serves families with children on the autism spectrum. Tirza is proud to be the mother of 3 wild teenagers, including her incredible son who is diagnosed with autism. Tirza's spirituality is one of many influences and teachings. Beginning with a Christian up-bringing and being raised on a Christian commune in her early childhood, she later expanded into more earth-based ways. While in her 20's Tirza was adopted into the Native American Church, where she learned from her relatives a way of living the "Beauty Way." During the 1990's and early 2000's, Tirza lived in San Francisco, Oakland and Berkeley, directing the Mystic Family Circus, which was a performance group dedicated to cultural awareness and bridge building. She worked with Cirque du Soleil, Burning Man, Reclaiming, Contraband, CELLspace and other Bay Area art collectives and non profits to provide conscious entertainment and "prayerformances" for the betterment of humankind and the planet. In 2012, Tirza helped to found the Buckeye Gathering, an ancestral skills gathering in Northern California which draws teachers and students of all ages to learn ancestral ways of tending the earth and survival skills. Tirza Dawn was the founder of yoga programming and the Ayurvedic Yoga Teacher Trainings at the dhyana Center of Ayurveda in Sebastopol, California, which operated a community center of healing and education from 2010 to 2020.

title: What About Age? Art Exhibit
description:
*What About Age?* art exhibit has arrived in Marin County! Originally displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows, this exhibit explores ageism through contemporary art, featuring works by both local youth and senior artists.

*What About Age?* is an art exhibit and educational initiative designed to challenge stereotypes about aging, address ageism and social isolation, and promote intergenerational dialogue through the lens of art.

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts (HCA) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

\- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

\- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

\- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed (144 sq in) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

\- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired (no alligator clips). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

\- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

Key Dates:

\- Entry Deadline: May 10, 2026 (9 PM)

\- Notification of Selection: By May 13, 2026

\- Shipped Work Deadline: Wednesday, May 27, 2026 (must include pre-paid return label)

\- Hand-Delivery: Sunday, May 31 (12–4 PM) and Monday, June 1 (11 AM–1 PM)

\- Exhibition Dates: June 4, 2026 – July 19, 2026

\- Opening Reception: Saturday, June 6, 2026 (4–6 PM)

\- Pick-up/Return Shipping: July 19 (12–4 PM) and July 20 (11 AM–1 PM); shipping the week of July 20.

Entry Fees:

\- Non-Members: $50 (1 entry), $55 (2 entries), $60 (3 entries). Includes a $60 yearly supporter membership.

\- Current Members: $40 (1 entry), $45 (2 entries), $50 (3 entries).

You’ll set short poems by hand, experiment with layout and typography, and print your work on the press—embracing the beautiful constraints and surprises of letterpress.

As the weeks progress, we’ll curate and print a collaborative chapbook featuring original poems from everyone in the group. The final result will be a shared, tactile publication that reflects a month of creative exchange, ink-stained hands, and collective storytelling.

No prior letterpress or poetry experience is required—just curiosity, openness, and a willingness to play with language and form. Whether you’re a seasoned poet or brand new to writing, this workshop offers space to experiment, connect, and make something meaningful together.

*All materials included. Participants will receive copies of the finished chapbook.*

title: Ketch Secor & Molly Tuttle
description:
Ketch is best known as the founder and frontman of Old Crow Medicine Show, a two-time Grammy Award-winning juggernaut whose triumphs include induction into the Grand Ole Opry, double-platinum certification, and world-wide touring. It is impossible to overstate the influence of Old Crow, whose literary songwriting, true-to-life roadside adventures, and high-octane live performances helped spur artistic shifts in country, Americana, folk, pop, and rock music spheres since the band’s formation in 1998. “Old Crow Medicine Show were the band that made me fall in love with country music,” says Marcus Mumford.

A prolific writer, wordsmith and storyteller, Ketch’s most familiar creation is “Wagon Wheel,” originally recorded by Old Crow Medicine and later by Darius Rucker. Co-written with Bob Dylan, “Wagon Wheel” is one of the top five best-selling country songs of all time. But his mastery of language doesn’t stop with song. From children’s books to musical theatre productions and from TEDx talks to New York Times’ opinion pieces, Ketch’s words take on many forms. “Ketch Secor is one of my favorite writers. Whether it’s songs, books, essays, radio scripts or letters to home, Ketch has a way of making the world spin a little smoother when he starts putting words together. His words never fail to enlighten and they always have the power to make me smile,” says Marty Stuart.

When it comes to American music, Ketch is a chosen steward and a torch bearer––as well as a questioner of the gatekeepers. Serving as an advisor, historical consultant, and featured speaker in Ken Burns’ acclaimed 2019 documentary Country Music, Ketch was a bridge between generations of country music makers and lovers, as he pushed for a wider lens and deeper understanding of the art form’s roots. “Ketch is a library, but he has this carnival-barker showman thing,” says Dave Rawlings.

title: The Wedding Present
description:
“The boy Gedge has written some of the best love songs of the Rock ‘n’ Roll Era. You may dispute this, but I’m right and you’re wrong!” John Peel.

The Wedding Present have had eighteen UK Top 40 hit singles… not bad for a band that has, from its inception, stubbornly refused to play the record industry’s game. That was back in 1985 when David Lewis Gedge boarded a National Express coach in London with 500 records packed into a pair of his mother's suitcases. In this fashion, the debut single GO OUT AND GET 'EM BOY! was collected from the pressing plant, delivered to the distribution company, and The Wedding Present was born. That pioneering spirit has been at the core of the band's philosophy ever since. From GEORGE BEST, "an unmitigated delight" \[NME\], the first full-length release on their own Reception Records onwards, the band has charted an appealing, if often eccentric, course of its very own.

With the early releases on their own label The Wedding Present acquired a reputation for bittersweet, breathtakingly honest love songs immersed in whirlwind guitars, so it was extraordinary that UKRAINSKI VISTUPI V JOHNA PEELA, with the band exploring traditional Eastern European folk music, should be the major label debut on RCA. “\(They\) carry off what is basically a bold experiment with verve” \[NME\]. However, this was soon followed by the more traditionally incendiary BIZARRO, “simply unbeatable” \[Melody Maker\] which featured their first hit single KENNEDY. Sounds Magazine said: “it’s their major label debut, but it’s a transition they’ve mastered beautifully”.

The next step, made with characteristically twisted Wedding Present logic, was to enlist noise-mongering \[and, at that point, relatively unknown\] sound engineer Steve Albini's aid at a time when everyone else was releasing ‘Madchester’ dance mixes. The resulting SEAMONSTERS, recorded in the snowy wilds of Minnesota in just 11 days, suggested a more thoughtful Wedding Present. The Guardian newspaper noted that: "Albini has given The Wedding Present considerable weight, with Gedge's voice trickling between banks of scowling guitars". Indeed, the singing ranged from sensual whispering to feverish screams.

The band came up with their next intriguing idea in 1992. By the end of December, The Wedding Present had released twelve singles, one per month, equalled Elvis Presley's 35 year old record for "most hits in one year", rekindled everyone's interest in that ultimate pop format, the 7" and led the NME to describe the band as "casually revolutionary and underhandedly unique". A gang of impressive names, including Ian Broudie from The Lightning Seeds and legendary Rolling Stones producer Jimmy Miller collaborated on the industry-challenging project, ultimately to be compiled on the two HIT PARADE albums and awarded "record of the week" by Tony Parsons in The Daily Telegraph.

WATUSI, produced by Steve Fisk \(a prime mover in the celebrated avant-garde scene of Seattle\), whisked the band off into another new area with its lo-fi pop, three-part a capella harmonies and Waikiki-ready surf strains. This “strong, multifaceted album” \[Select\], sprinkled with 60s and 70s pastiches, was described by some critics as their most varied and dynamic to date. “Watusi is \(their\) ‘White Album’, a late period re-assessment of their sound that finds them doing what they do best” \[Melody Maker\].

In 1995, the band released yet another 7" single, SUCKER, and completed a British tour with two drummers. Although the record sold several thousand copies and reached No.3 in The Festive 50 \(the late BBC DJ John Peel's end of year listeners' poll\) you won't see it in any other charts, because, typically, it was only available at the concerts or by mail order.

The band returned to a more traditional form of record distribution with the car themed MINI, "a gem of a record" \[Melody Maker\] in which Gedge cloaked his tales of love, lust and infidelity with automobile symbolism in what can only be described as a concept album. To commemorate this release, the band played at the BBC's Sound City Event, which was held that year in Leeds, the group’s home town. During the concert, the winner of a prize draw was announced, and a lucky Wedding Present fan became the owner of a real life classic Austin Mini motorcar provided \(and delivered!\) by the band.

For the next full length LP, the group decided to apply a decade’s worth of studio experience and produce the record themselves. Thus, the Top 40 album SATURNALIA was released by Cooking Vinyl to a flurry of critical approval. The NME exclaimed that "David Gedge has just written one of the best pop albums of the year" while The Melody Maker noted that in the new recordings, which were completed in the London studios belonging to The Cocteau Twins, you could "hear an experimentalism that would send half of New York back to the lab".

It was at this point in 1997 that Gedge started work on a new project called CINERAMA. A fittingly titled outfit, Cinerama indulged Gedge's love of film music from John Barry to Blaxploitation via Ennio Morricone. Cinerama started life as a duo, Gedge and his girlfriend Sally Murrell, together with a shifting line-up of collaborators. 1998's VA VA VOOM “turbo-driven melodies and bittersweet vignettes taking in everything from John Barry to the Zombies” \[The Times\] featured The Church's Marty Wilson-Piper and Emma Pollock from The Delgados. Then, in 1999, Gedge rescued the rhythm section of the disbanded Goya Dress \(Terry de Castro and Simon Pearson\) and combined them with Wedding Present guitarist Simon Cleave. From 2000 the line-up remained relatively steady, apart from Finnish drummer Kari Paavola later replacing Pearson and Murrell’s eventual retirement from live performance.

Surely on pace to rival the abundant shelf filling of The Wedding Present, Cinerama released a clutch of singles in support of their debut LP, as well as a number prior to 2000's Steve Albini-recorded DISCO VOLANTE “dangerously, seductively sweet” \[Melody Maker\]. Notable were the heart-rending SUPERMAN \(complete with alternative Spanish take\) and the six and a half minute epic HEALTH AND EFFICIENCY \(also available in French!\).

The third Cinerama studio album, TORINO \(released in 2002\), was much darker than the first two, with Gedge returning to a guitar driven sound and deciding to write predominantly about infidelity. “Cinerama are escaping the shadow of Gedge’s illustrious indie-legend past. Torino is a giant beast of adulterous lyrical fantasies, cult soundtrack flourishes and the screams of Albini-engineered guitars” \[Uncut\].

At the end of 2002, Gedge and Murrell unexpectedly split up, and he decided to leave Leeds, his home for the preceding twenty-four years, and move to Seattle in the USA. Following the end of this fourteen-year relationship, Gedge began writing a collection of songs apparently influenced by his despair over the split. TAKE FOUNTAIN, the resultant album, was recorded in Seattle by Steve Fisk \[who also produced WATUSI, The Wedding Present’s 1994 LP\] and released, perhaps ironically, on St. Valentine’s Day 2005. This saw Gedge reviving The Wedding Present name for the first album since 1996’s SATURNALIA to a torrent of critical acclaim. TAKE FOUNTAIN “is as eloquent an emotional discourse as he has mustered. Gedge has never before assimilated harsh rock textures to orchestral arrangements with such power.” \[Mojo\]. “Gedge hasn’t sounded this belligerently broken-hearted since 1987’s MY FAVOURITE DRESS” \[Uncut\]. “Fans have long since recognised Gedge as more poet than pop star. Like Byron without the marsh fever, TAKE FOUNTAIN confirms his status as an extraordinary songwriter” \[The Times\].

In the wake of TAKE FOUNTAIN’s success, and after almost an eight-year hiatus, The Wedding Present set out on a mammoth twenty month concert tour of Europe and North America which included most of the major festivals and ended in November 2006. In December of that year Gedge relocated to Hollywood, California, where he is currently living and writing but ventured back across the Atlantic in October 2007 when The Wedding Present performed the GEORGE BEST album live as part of a George Best “Twentieth Anniversary” Tour of Europe. Following that tour the band reassembled in at Steve Albini’s Electrical Audio studio in Chicago to record “El Rey”.

Now back in the UK, April 2009 saw Gedge collaborating with the BBC Big Band for the bi-annual FUSE Festival which was held back in his home town of Leeds. For the event he performed Wedding Present and Cinerama songs backed by eighteen world class musicians including legendary 'James Bond' trumpeter Derek Watkins. In what proved to be a busy yet unusual year for Gedge he also made his debut as a radio DJ in Texas, released his bass player’s solo album on his label Scopitones and launched his own annual self-curated mini-festival, AT THE EDGE OF THE SEA, in Brighton, England. Also in 2009, two Take Fountain songs, I’M FROM FURTHER NORTH THAN YOU and RINGWAY TO SEATAC, appeared in the award winning independent film Skills Like This.

In 2012 The Wedding present released VALENTINA to further rave reviews. Of the album, which was mixed in L.A. by Grammy award winning producer Andrew Scheps, and also came out in book form, Magnet \[USA\] said: "guitars meander before slicing, the rhythm section is taut and Gedge hits all of his favourite topics - love, lust and spite - often in the same three or four minutes". 2012 also saw the release of a new comic book series, TALES FROM THE WEDDING PRESENT, which, Gedge has hinted, is essentially his memoirs in graphic novel style. Another notable release in 2012 was the '4 Chansons EP' which saw Gedge singing four tracks in French and which was followed in 2013 by the '4 Lieder EP' in German and in 2014 by 'EP 4 Cân' in Welsh!

In what turned out to be a huge and comprehensive reassessment of the band, 2014 saw Edsel Records re-releasing eight Wedding Present albums in critically acclaimed multi-disc 'extended' editions which brought together a wealth of historic recordings, radio sessions and videos.

Such has been the unpredictable nature of Gedge's career over the years, hardly anyone could have been surprised when he announced yet another remarkable project in 2015. Collaborating with Spanish indie legend Pedro Vigil he decided to 're-imagine' The Wedding Present's VALENTINA album as Cinerama. The resulting recording was also entitled VALENTINA and, with its "musical set pieces and vocal nuances fine enough to rival Bacharach and David",  was described as "a truly sparkling and uplifting concerto for the modern age" by Vive Le Rock Magazine. Cinerama celebrated the release of this remarkable album with live performances in London & Barcelona and for BBC Radio 6 Music using additional musicians including a string quartet, brass and a flautist. The London concert was subsequently released on CD & DVD as 'Live 2015'.

In 2016 The Wedding Present released their ninth studio album, 'GOING, GOING...', which featured references to Gedge's previous works, including self-referential lyrical moments, and has been described as his masterpiece. Loosely based on a road trip across the U.S.A., the double LP was described by Louder Than War as “A remarkable album. A joy from start to finish." Allmusic added that “It's hard to deny the brilliance of a band that can crank out an album as passionate, hook-filled and flat-out fiery as this” while The Quietus described it as “A wonderful album and a fine addition the canon.” Q Magazine noted that “The Wedding Present have never been afraid to wander off in strange directions... \[and\] their ninth long-player is in a similarly experimental vein.”

title: Clay Exploration Evenings: Lvl 2 — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Clay Exploration Evenings: Lvl 2, 4/30

  
    
      
        
          $255.00
        
      
    
  

Thursdays, April 30 - June 4, 2026 (6 sessions) 6 - 8:30pm$210 + $45 clay fee (pre-registration required)This course is designed for students wishing to explore hand-building techniques at an intermediate to advanced level and delve deeper into refining their clay skills. Each session will start with a demonstration of a specific technique related to functional and/or decorative pottery. Participants are invited to explore new ideas and to try pieces that might be of a more challenging nature. Some of what we can explore are freeform coil pots, soft slab work, hard slab technique, a variety of sculptural techniques and a sampling of the many stamping, carving and textural surface treatments on clay. We will investigate ways to use slips and glaze that will add color to the forms we create.About the Instructor: Michael Citrino has had a love affair with clay for over 50 years. After his college experience at California College of Arts and Crafts with Viola Frey and further work at Humboldt State University with Lew Merrick, he ran a stained glass business for 18 years. Michael and his wife left for Turkey in 1991 to teach in International Schools. For 26 years he taught K-12 art, including Ceramics, Drawing, Photography, Design and Sculpture at schools in six different countries. He started clay programs for High School and Middle School students at three of those schools. At four of these schools he offered after school and weekend ceramics sessions for teachers and parents. Michael’s work ranges from the traditional to the experimental and a wide swath in between. His approach to teaching is to help students explore the playful nature of the clay room and nurture a love for the possibilities that medium presents.

description:
Pawsport Napa Valley 2026

PURCHASE YOUR PAWSPORT HERE: https://napahumane.org/events/pawsport/

What Your Pawsport Unlocks: • One complimentary wine tasting per Pawsport holder at each participating winery • Access to a curated lineup of dog-friendly Napa Valley wineries

How to Use Your Pawsport: • Your Pawsport is valid March 1–April 30, 2026 with one tasting per person, per winery • Be sure to check each winery’s hours and reservation requirements before visiting, as many locations do require reservations

Your Impact: Every Pawsport supports Napa Humane’s Power of Prevention—helping fund lifesaving spay and neuter surgeries and preventive care that reduce overpopulation and prevent suffering. Together, Pawsport supporters help make it possible to fund up to 246 days of lifesaving surgery each year, creating a lasting impact for animal welfare in Napa County.

Ready to Sip for a Cause? Grab your Pawsport, explore Napa Valley wineries, and enjoy complimentary tastings all while helping protect pets through prevention-focused care. Don’t forget to share your adventures using \#PawsportNapaValley and by tagging @napahumane.

Thank you for helping make Napa Valley a more compassionate place for pets and the people who love them—we can’t wait to raise a glass with you this spring! 🐾🍷

title: INTO THE LIGHT: Light-filled aintings by Katy Boggs
description:
Katy's paintings are an exploration of light—how it shapes form, reveals color, and defines what we see.

"I am drawn to moments where light is felt as much as seen: filtering through dense leaves, towering in the crowns of trees, glinting off cresting waves, or softening into the quiet glow of a sunset. Light is everywhere; without it, there is no seeing. Beyond its physical presence, it also carries a deeper resonance as a symbol of hope. In a time of uncertainty, this work seeks to bring light into the image, both visually and metaphorically."

Reception: April 25, 4 to 6 pm.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma County artist, Karen Miller, presents The Poetic Landscape, pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments, a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. \(707\) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    www.upstairsart gallery.net 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

Thursdays 11 am - 1 pm

Drawing a Portrait is Challenging and Fun!

Portraits have always been my forte. I spent many years as a quick sketch portrait artist and later studied classical and impressionistic portraits.

This class will have projects and demos covering basic head structure and features, how to get a likeness and capture those qualities that make a portrait unique. We will also explore different portrait styles in art history.

Using photo references, we will begin with pencil and charcoal before using color. Students can work on their own projects as well. Beginning to advanced students.

title: Small Wonders
description:
Call for Art: Small Wonders

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts \(HCA\) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed \(144 sq in\) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired \(no alligator clips\). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

Key Dates:

- Entry Deadline: May 10, 2026 \(9 PM\)

- Notification of Selection: By May 13, 2026

- Shipped Work Deadline: Wednesday, May 27, 2026 \(must include pre-paid return label\)

- Hand-Delivery: Sunday, May 31 \(12–4 PM\) and Monday, June 1 \(11 AM–1 PM\)

- Exhibition Dates: June 4, 2026 – July 19, 2026

- Opening Reception: Saturday, June 6, 2026 \(4–6 PM\)

- Pick-up/Return Shipping: July 19 \(12–4 PM\) and July 20 \(11 AM–1 PM\); shipping the week of July 20.

Entry Fees:

- Non-Members: $50 \(1 entry\), $55 \(2 entries\), $60 \(3 entries\). Includes a $60 yearly supporter membership.

- Current Members: $40 \(1 entry\), $45 \(2 entries\), $50 \(3 entries\).

$25 – One Bag or Doll Entry $40 – Two Bags or Dolls entryTransform plastic dolls and create upcycled bags from trash into unique art. Join our hands-on Trashion workshop for the Gallery 212 Exhibit and Auction.

About the Class

This hands-on workshop invites participants to rescue and reinvent plastic dolls \(Barbies, Kens, and dolls that are under 12 inches\) often destined for landfills, where they can take 20 to 500 years to decompose. As part of Trashion Season, join us for the beloved Gallery 212 Exhibit and Auction \(April 3 – 25\) where discarded materials are transformed into small-scale works of art for a good cause. Together, we’ll reclaim these forgotten figures and reimagine them as expressive, one-of-a-kind artworks for submission to the gallery exhibit and auction. New this year: Bags! In addition to dolls, we’re expanding the exhibit to include bags—think totes, clutches, cross bagsm fanny packs, coin purses, and backpacks. Just like the Trashion runway, the only rule is that your piece must be made from unconventional materials and/or upcycled/used textiles. Participants will have access to access to sewing machines, hot glue guns, irons, hair dryers and other creative tools as well of a wide selection of trash and upcycled materials to bring their vision to life. BYOT \(Bring your own trash\) is also welcome and encouraged! The workshop registration is your application fee to the gallery exhibit! Come play, experiment, and collaborate while contributing to a dynamic gallery exhibit that raises funds for Sonoma Community Center programming through the auction. It’s a joy to see your art find a new home—and to be part of a creative community turning trash into treasure.

Thank you to Recology Sonoma-Marin for donating Barbies & Dolls for our gallery exhibit every year.

Express joy through drawing. Build skills in sketching, composition & landscapes. Boost focus, creativity, connection & well-being.

About the Class

When we feel a sense of joy, it is natural to express that feeling from our body. We may use our voice and sing, we may dance, and we may use our hands in creative expression. By drawing we leave a mark of that expression. This course is shaped with skill building exercises to improve eye-hand coordination with quick sketching and gesture drawing and practices of learning to see how to abstract shapes of light and dark for developing strong compositions. We will focus on landscape imagery from photos and drawing from setups in the studio. Drawing outside of class will be encouraged but not required. There are many health benefits from drawing such as: improvements in cognitive focus, freedom of expression with your hands, the satisfaction that comes from seeing the world in a different way, the social camaraderie of acceptance in the studio, and the joy of doing something with your hands.

Required Materials List

A good size sketch book for multimedia

Newsprint drawing pad \(12” x 18” or 18” x 24”\)

Black pencils, 6B soft

Compressed charcoal sticks, black and white

Eraser, kneaded rubber

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting March 2025, we ask that every attending member pay a $1 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!

title: Deep Sky Astrophotography Image Capture (class 3 of 3)
description:
Do you understand the fundamentals of deep sky image processing, and would you now like to learn how to capture your own raw data?  This class is for you!

Note that this class is designed for students who have already attended the RFO “Deep Sky Astrophotography Processing Class” or for students who already have experience with basic astrophotography image processing.

What you will learn in this class:
-    A refresher on the fundamentals of Deep Sky Astrophotography
-    A review of the equipment and techniques required for deep sky image capture
-    Hands-on experience capturing deep sky images at the Robert Ferguson Observatory
-    An opportunity to discuss techniques, share images and get feedback from docents and fellow students

Please note, this workshop is meant as a 3-class series. It is highly recommended to purchase tickets for all three days.

Please note, class 1 and 3 are virtual. A Zoom link will be sent to participants prior to the class. Class 2 will be in person at the Robert Ferguson Observatory. 

Get more information and purchase tickets at rfo.simpletix.com.

title: Samba no Pé - First Class
description:
Get ready to feel the rhythm and energy of Rio de Janeiro! Samba no Pé \(Samba in the Foot\) is the captivating solo style of samba danced in the streets and at Carnival, known for its rapid, intricate footwork and infectious hip movements.

You will learn

The Basic Step: You will master the signature quick-quick-slow rhythm that defines Samba no Pé.

Arm & Hip Styling: You will learn how to add the authentic flair, movement, and energy that makes Brazilian samba so captivating.

Technique & Posture: You will receive tips on proper body alignment to help you dance longer, faster, and more safely.

Rhythm & Musicality: You will learn how to connect your movement directly to the irresistible beat of the bateria \(the samba drum section\).

This class is perfect for anyone looking to connect with the vibrant spirit of Brazil, improve coordination, and get a fantastic workout—all while learning the foundational steps of this iconic dance. No partner or prior dance experience is required! Just bring your enthusiasm and comfortable shoes!

Date & Time: Thursdays @6:30PM – 7:30PM

Address: 4140 Redwood Highway \#8 San Rafael, CA

Note: Arrive 10 minutes before. No floor marking shoe soles allowed.

title: Yotes
description:
Yotes combines his rich baritone vocals with an energetic delivery, playing a mix of songs from 1950’s country, 1980’s neo rockabilly, modern Americana, and many genres and eras in between.  He mixes songs by Johnny Cash, The Stray Cats, The Blasters, and Murder By Death with his own compositions.  Old favorites are interspersed with some of his favorite songs by friends and up-and-coming artists he’s met through the years.

 

Over the past fifteen years Yotes has developed his solo show, leaning on over two decades of performing experience in several bands ranging from high energy punk and rockabilly to soulful country, folk, and blues acts.  During that time his solo shows evolved from being a convenient testbed for new songs and exploring different styles to a full-time traveling act.  Yotes’s solo performances are tribute to the artists and music that have influenced him, a respectful nod to some of his favorite contemporaries, and an opportunity to share his own creations with live music fans everywhere!

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma County artist, Karen Miller, presents The Poetic Landscape, pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.” 

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments, a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Small Wonders
description:
Call for Art: Small Wonders

Some of the most exquisite beauty can be captured in the smallest of images and objects: the iridescence of a hummingbird in flight, a millefiori paperweight, Faberge eggs, or a miniature woven basket. These pieces are modest in size but powerful in creativity and expression.

Healdsburg Center for the Arts \(HCA\) invites artists to submit paintings, original fine art prints, collage, mixed media, drawings, fiber arts, sculptures, ceramics, and jewelry for this exhibition.

Application Requirements:

- Platform: All applications must be submitted via EntryThingy

- Eligibility: Work must be original and completed within the past two years. Photos in the application must represent the actual work intended for exhibition.

- Size/Weight: Artwork must not exceed 12" x 12" unframed \(144 sq in\) or 196 sq in framed. Maximum weight is 40 lbs.

- Display: 2-D pieces must be securely wired \(no alligator clips\). 3-D work must be stable; artists are responsible for on-site assembly if required.

- Sales: All work must be for sale. HCA retains a 40% commission; artists receive 60%. Please list retail prices only.

Key Dates:

- Entry Deadline: May 10, 2026 \(9 PM\)

- Notification of Selection: By May 13, 2026

- Shipped Work Deadline: Wednesday, May 27, 2026 \(must include pre-paid return label\)

- Hand-Delivery: Sunday, May 31 \(12–4 PM\) and Monday, June 1 \(11 AM–1 PM\)

- Exhibition Dates: June 4, 2026 – July 19, 2026

- Opening Reception: Saturday, June 6, 2026 \(4–6 PM\)

- Pick-up/Return Shipping: July 19 \(12–4 PM\) and July 20 \(11 AM–1 PM\); shipping the week of July 20.

Entry Fees:

- Non-Members: $50 \(1 entry\), $55 \(2 entries\), $60 \(3 entries\). Includes a $60 yearly supporter membership.

- Current Members: $40 \(1 entry\), $45 \(2 entries\), $50 \(3 entries\).

title: Monica Da Silva & Complicated Animals
description:
Monica da Silva grew up living between The United States and Belém, Brazil, a city on the Amazon River. A love of travel and foreign language helped to forge her unique sound. 

 

Paralleling her life, da Silva's music contains an eclectic mix of Brazilian and American influences. Her sound can be classified as International Fusion, as it is heavily influenced by Brazilian music, namely Bossa Nova, but also incorporates elements of Lounge, Electronica, Indie Pop, and Worldbeat. Da Silva brings her cultural diversity to her songs, smoothly flowing between English, Portuguese, and Spanish.

 

In 2010, da Silva released her album "Brasilissima" . The record featured songs in both of her native languages - English and Portuguese. The first single "Aí Então", “was chosen by Putumayo World Music to be included on their compilation “Brazilian Beat”. The upbeat, psychedelic track "That's Not The Way" was chosen by the music director of ESPN to be played during the programming of The FIFA World Cup in 2014, alongside major recording artists Coldplay, Sérgio Mendes, Pitbull, Jennifer Lopez, The Black Eyed Peas, Stan Getz, and Astrud Gilberto. 

Da Silva's single "Soldado de Amor" \(2017\) has been featured in the BBC One series "The Replacement”, in the Paramount Network series "American Woman", and in a 2019 campaign for the designer Tory Burch.

Her music has also been featured in the series "Heartland", and in an ad for Patron Tequila. She is currently recording a new, full-length solo album, as well as writing and recording with her project, Complicated Animals.

title: Nancy Fawson Music
description:
Nancy Fawson is a powerhouse Bay Area-based vocalist and songwriter whose musical roots run deep in soul, R&B and rock. Raised on the iconic sounds of Sam Cooke, Etta James, Aretha Franklin, Chaka Khan, Stevie Wonder, and Amy Winehouse, Nancy’s musical influences have left an indelible imprint on her voice and style. With a unique, soulful tone and a passion for heartfelt expression, Nancy connects with her audience on a profound level—delivering each song with purity, emotion, and authenticity.

Nancy’s vocal range spans across a variety of genres, including soul, funk, blues, R&B, and rock, allowing her to bring versatility to every performance. Whether performing with a duo or full band, she engages audiences with her compelling stage presence and soulful delivery.

As the lead singer of the popular Marin-based blues, soul, and funk band Corner Pocket, Nancy continues to captivate crowds with her raw energy and dedication to the craft. In addition to live performances, she is also available for recording session work, offering her talents as both a lead and background vocalist.

With a sound that blends classic influences with modern flair, Nancy Fawson is an artist whose voice you won’t soon forget.

title: Callie Watts
description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. Over time, she’s had the honor of opening for acts such as Bootsy Collins, Elvin Bishop, Huey Lewis and The News, War, Ozomatli, Bill Champlin, Booker T, and the B52s. Callie continues to perform frequently as an acoustic solo artist, focusing on developing a core audience and a buzz for her original material. title: KC Johns & Creed Fisher
description:
If you listen to just a few tracks from his latest album, you might think Creed Fisher was born with a guitar in his hand. One after another his songs remain relevant today, yet steeped with tradition classics that everyone else already knows and you don’t want to miss. Clearly he’s sharing his own stories, with experiences that range from great victories to deep battle scars. 

Fisher hails from Odessa, TX,  where his family’s roots trace back to his granddad, who was highly involved in the oil game back in the fifties. However, Fisher took on a different passion when he started playing football at the age of 10, which eventually led to the Minor Leagues for 9 years. 

But, as his football career came to a close, Fisher also saw his marriage of twelve years come to an end. It was at this point he decided to do some serious “soul searching”. Fisher tells us that the music simply “found him” during this time. He picked up a guitar in 2010 and never let it go; and after touring tirelessly for 4 years, Fisher moved from West Texas to a small town outside of San Antonio, TX, where he put together a new band, and picked up where he left off.

Fisher’s second album "Ain't Scared To Bleed" went Top 30 on the ITunes Country charts and continues to be embraced by fans all around the world. When it came to his 3rd album "Rednecks Like Us" it was reviewed by Country Music People magazine and got 4 out of 5 stars. Here is what they had to say...

“Creed Fisher sings and writes with the confidence and authority of someone who has been at it for a hell of a lot longer than 6 years. He is at his strongest on the ballads, but tackles the ‘angry redneck’ stuff just as well. There’s the odd moment when it can all get a bit crashy and loud for me, but I’d say the same about Hank Jr. All things considered, this is very impressive indeed and I’d like to see Creed Fisher go far.

Friends and fans alike anxiously await Creed Fisher’s release of his 4th album. There is no denying that Fisher is truly speaking from passion when it comes to his music. Fisher is the guy you meet that you feel like you’ve known all your life and his music feels like the songs you’ve been singing since you first discovered music. His lyrics

are comfortable; his story, genuine; his spirit, humble and his talent, undeniable.”

Country Music People Magazine 

- September 2016

title: Postcards - Spring 2026 Concert Series
description:
The Occidental Community Choir puts on live concerts featuring an eclectic mix of locally composed music, classical and contemporary choral pieces, poetry, and spoken word from our community in the redwoods of Northern California.

The Occidental Community Choir invites audiences to its Spring concert series, Postcards, a musical journey through memory, connection, and the moments that shape our lives.

In times that can feel uncertain or isolating, even small gestures of connection—a postcard, a call, a simple message saying “I’m thinking of you”—can remind us that we are not alone. Postcards is built around that spirit of reaching out. Each piece in the program serves as a musical postcard: a snapshot from a particular time and place, carrying stories of joy, longing, hope, and reflection.

Some of these musical postcards arrive bright and sun-drenched; others carry the weathered edges of memory. Together they form a collection of moments that remind us our lives are measured not only in years, but in the experiences that stay with us and the ones we share with others. Through song, the choir becomes both sender and recipient—offering voices as messages of care, presence, and connection. Postcards is a reminder that even in difficult times, music can help us reach across distance and say something simple and powerful: you matter, you are connected, and you are not alone.

Join the Occidental Community Choir this spring for an evening of music that carries stories, memories, and hope into a weary and waiting world.

About the Artist: Ping Zhong’s artistic practice is a continuous exploration of regeneration—of materials, forms, and cultural narratives. She investigates the dialogue between ancient Chinese pottery and contemporary visual language, using wheel-throwing, hand-building, and sculpture to create works in which history and personal growth converge. This reinterpretation of classical forms is not only an artistic method, but also a philosophical inquiry into the harmony between past and future. Deeply motivated to uncover the potential within clay, Ping pushes the boundaries of design and technique. Her work reflects on universal themes: the individual’s place within the community, the relationship between essence and appearance, and the evolving connection between nature and society. Through these explorations, she seeks to create art that resonates across cultures.

If you have wanted to try out this fairly new and very popular way to make your own papers, whether you are an experienced artist or simply curious about the process, this workshop will provide plenty of creative inspiration and expert insights.

During the 3-hours workshop, you will learn the fundamentals of mono-printing with a gel plate,
including an in-depth look at the essential supplies needed. Magdalena will discuss different
types of plates and brayers, as well as the wide range of acrylic paints and inks. You will learn the basics of color theory to ensure great results for your projects.

You will get to try out many fun techniques on different papers. Magdalena will introduce various papers for gel printing, including white copy paper, calligraphy paper, deli paper, marker paper, and more each offering unique effects.

The workshop will also explore tools for making marks and textures, from found objects to store-bought supplies. Magdalena will demonstrate how to use stencils - both handmade and purchased, along with unconventional tools like silicone scrapers, scrapers, bubble wrap, buttons, yarn, and cardboard to create stunning patterns.

She will also cover techniques to embellish your prints incorporating acrylic pens, Inktense pencils and other techniques.
Additionally, Magdalena will provide expert guidance on cleaning, caring for, and storing gel plates to ensure their longevity. To wrap up the session, she will showcase creative ways to use your printed papers, including ideas for collages, handmade cards, and art journals, along with a take-home list of even more ways to incorporate your gel prints into future projects. Whether you are looking to refine your skills or try something new, this workshop promises to be an engaging and educational experience. Come explore the endless possibilities of gel printing.

title: Expressive Portraits
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson

Thursdays 11 am - 1 pm

Beginning March 19

Fee: $30/Session/Ongoing

Drawing a Portrait is Challenging and Fun!

Portraits have always been my forte. I spent many years as a quick sketch portrait artist and later studied classical and impressionistic portraits.

This class will have projects and demos covering basic head structure and features, how to get a likeness and capture those qualities that make a portrait unique. We will also explore different portrait styles in art history.

Using photo references, we will begin with pencil and charcoal before using color. Students can work on their own projects as well. Beginning to advanced students.

To enroll please call or text Suzanne at 707-888-2083

Marshall House Project (Voted 2025’s Best Funk Band of the North Bay by The Bohemian) is a driving soul funk outfit with one foot rooted deep in the pockets of the past and the other fearlessly exploring the deep fry of the future. location: Rileystreet Art Supply,1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

You can also visit Eva's website at: http://evamautner.com http://evamautner.com evamautner.com

title: Cosmos & Cocoa
description:
Join us for an unforgettable evening of stargazing, exploration, and cozy treats at Cosmos and Cocoa! This event brings together the wonders of the cosmos with a warm cup of cocoa.

Kick off the night with a short, guided hike along a portion our captivating Planet Walk, where you'll encounter scale models of many of our solar system’s planets, each with its own unique story. As the stars begin to sparkle, we’ll gather for an in-depth stargazing and storytelling session led by experienced astronomers who’ll point out constellations, planets, and celestial objects. 

The event’s highlight is telescope viewing through our powerful observatory telescopes, providing a chance to get up-close views of the astronomical objects visible in the sky that month which could include the Moon’s craters, Saturn’s rings, Jupiter’s moons, and distant galaxies. Experts will be on hand to answer questions and guide you through the night sky’s best features.

And of course, stay warm with complimentary cups of rich cocoa as you marvel at the universe above. Whether you're an avid stargazer or a curious beginner, Cosmos and Cocoa promises an evening filled with wonder and warmth.

No prior experience necessary, and all ages are welcome. Dress warmly and bring a flashlight with a red light setting (no white light allowed). Red light flashlights will also be available for purchase.

 Register at rfo.simpletix.com.

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: JaM Cellar Presents Eric Johnson
description:
May 13, 2026
PURCHASE TICKETS HERE  
Doors 7pm/ Show 8pm
Ages: 12+ 
One of the most outstanding instrumentalists in rock over the past 40 years, Texas guitarist Eric Johnson was already a legend before he recorded his first album. By the early 1980s, many celebrated guitarists were singing the praises of this skinny kid from Austin with the mind-melting chops. Comparisons were made to such guitar heroes as Jeff Beck and Jimi Hendrix and when he joined the ‘70s Austin fusion band Electromagnets they were being hailed as “the Mahavishnu Orchestra of Texas”. 
With the release of his highly-anticipated 1986 solo debut album Tones, the underground guitar legend finally emerged onto the scene fully-formed. It landed him on the cover of Guitar Player magazine, which hailed the album as a “majestic debut”, and earned him his first Grammy nomination for the song “Zap”. With the release of his follow up album, 1990’s platinum-selling Ah Via Musicom, which contained the Grammy Award winning song “Cliffs of Dover”, Eric Johnson became a bona fide international guitar phenomenon. 
The New Age Music Guide once opined that “Eric Johnson plays guitar the way Michelangelo painted ceilings: with a colorful vibrancy that’s more real than life” while Rolling Stone included him in their list of the 100 Greatest Guitarists of the 21st century. A dynamic singer as well as an incredibly gifted guitarist, a pianist and a prolific songwriter, Eric has been featured on the cover of countless guitar magazines around the world while also racking up critical accolades along the way. 
Since 1986 Eric has released seventeen albums, in addition to albums with other artists such as Eclectic with jazz guitarist Mike Stern, and the platinum-selling G3 Live with Joe Satriani and Steve Vai. Eric has received eight Grammy nominations along with numerous other recognitions, awards and wins in various polls and magazines. 
Among Johnson’s many accolades are a GRAMMY award in 1992 for “Cliffs of Dover” as Best Rock Instrumental Performance, lifetime induction into the Guitar Player Gallery of Greats, and his listing among the “100 Greatest Guitarists of the 20th Century” by Musician magazine. In his hometown of Austin Texas, a city full of guitarists, the readers of the Austin Chronicle voted Eric Johnson the city’s “Best Electric Guitarist” and “Best Acoustic Guitarist” in their yearly poll year after year. They also named him “Electric Guitarist of the Decade” and one of the top five “Musicians of the Decade”. In February 2024 Eric was honored with induction into the Texas Heritage Songwriters Association Hall of Fame. 
2023 found Eric on his ‘Treasure Tour’, 67 US dates that were split between a Spring and a Fall tour. In January and February 2024 Eric joined the ‘G3 Reunion Tour’ with Joe Satriani and Steve Vai, and the resulting new live album from the tour will be released in January 2025. In August 2024 he heads out for a run of dates in the north and northeast including the Backroads Blues Festival in New York. In September and October 2024 Eric was a featured performer on the ‘Experience Hendrix 2024 Tour’, crossing the country from Washington state to Florida, and then rejoined in March and April 2025 for the ‘Experience Hendrix 2025 Tour’ throughout the east and northeast USA and Canada. 
Over the course of more than four decades, Eric Johnson has been traveling on a prolific odyssey. Along the way, his creations have cross-pollinated the various musical genres which include rock, blues, jazz, fusion, soul, folk, new-age, classical, and even country. Inevitably EJ says it best himself in sharing that regardless of the genre “It really boils down to the music and the song at the end of the day”, he explains. “The most important thing for me is to grow musically and make a more expansive and meaningful artistic statement with every new project”.

Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes

Smith Story Wine Cellars, based in Sonoma County, is the labor of love for Eric and Alison, who bring their combined 40+ years in the wine industry to the venture. Born out of their shared passion for wines during their tenure at K&L Wine Merchants, the couple founded the winery after eloping in Hawaii in 2013. Eric’s expertise lies in wine buying and retail management, specifically in European wines, while Ali excels in hospitality, marketing, and sales, providing a complete wine-supply-chain approach.
